#3595. GTA 6 Owner Take-Two Is Not Interested In Selling Itself After EA Goes Private For $55 Billion

Recently, the gaming giant Electronic Arts was taken private in a $55 billion sale to an investor consortium led by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund. Could GTA 6 owner Take-Two be the next big company that gets acquired? Don't bet on it, CEO Strauss Zelnick says.

Speaking to David Rubenstein, Zelnick said Take-Two's business results have proven that it "can do very well as an independent company."

He said Take-Two's business is already "at scale" and healthy enough financially with a "terrific balance sheet," as he put it.

"We are not in a place where we need to be part of a bigger organization to be competitive. And in the entertainment business, scale matters," he said.

Zelnick said companies that do less than a billion in annual revenue might have issues with developing, marketing, and distributing games at scale. Not only that, but companies that don't generate a lot of money might not be able to survive the realities of the creative business, in which sometimes your product flops.

"But once you're over a billion dollars in annual revenue, and we're way beyond that point. Our guidance is $8 billion to $8.2 billion this fiscal year, additional scale doesn't seem to help you succeed."

In early 2008, Electronic Arts privately pursued a buyout of Take-Two, but after the GTA and BioShock company rejected it, EA went public in an attempt to get a deal done. Later that year, EA abandoned its plans to try to buy Take-Two after the GTA company said it was worth more and EA refused to increase its bid.

In 2019, it was rumored that Sony was attempting to buy Take-Two, but that was ultimately deemed to be unconfirmed market chatter and not a formal bid.

Take-Two has a market cap of more than $42 billion, and that is expected to grow in the year ahead, so it would seemingly take a lot of money to convince Take-Two to sell. Going forward, Zelnick has teased that new GTA games could release even faster, and that could be a positive for the company's financials.

GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. Preloading is underway now, and that's good news because the game has a massive file size.

#3594. Taylor Swift Jokes About Being '0 for 8' for Grammys Song of the Year

Taylor Swift is finding humor in never winning the Grammys’ Song of the Year category.

The Recording Academy tapped Swift, 36, to help announce some of the nominations for the 2027 Grammys on Monday, November 16, which resulted in the pop star reflecting on her own history with the awards show.

“I’m very honored that the Grammys have asked me to be here to help reveal the last two categories for the Grammy nominations,” Swift, 36, said during Monday’s livestream.

She continued, “But I first wanted to start off by saying congratulations to anyone who is nominated for a Grammy this year in any category, because what this means is that your peers, your fellow musicians, producers, engineers, artists, writers, they love what you made.”

From Swift’s perspective, “that’s the coolest feeling in the world.” She noted in her message that she hopes the nominees “have a really wonderful day.”

“The last two categories to be announced, one of them I’ve had a lot of luck in. The other one I’m 0 for 8,” she said. “Here are the nominees for Album and Song of the Year.”

Swift earned her first Song of the Year nomination at the Grammys in 2010 for “You Belong With Me.” She has since received several additional nods with 2015’s “Shake It Off,” 2016’s “Blank Space,” 2020’s “Lover,” 2021’s “Cardigan,” 2023’s “All Too Well (10 Minute Version) (The Short Film),” 2024’s “Anti-Hero” and 2025’s “Fortnight.” She also received a nomination for the upcoming 2027 Grammys with “I Knew It, I Knew You,” a track off the Toy Story 5 soundtrack.

In the Album of the Year category, has been nominated seven times, winning for Fearless in 2010, 1989 in 2016, Folklore in 2021 and Midnights in 2024.

This year, Swift is also up for a trophy for Best Pop Duo/Group Performance with “The Life of a Showgirl” featuring Sabrina Carpenter, Record of the Year with “The Fate of Ophelia,” Album of the Year with The Life of a Showgirl and Best Song Written for Visual Media with “I Knew It, I Knew You.”

The 69th annual Grammys will be presented on February 7, 2027, at Los Angeles’ Crypto.com Arena, airing live on ABC. The broadcast will also be streamed on Disney+ and Hulu.

Ahead of the 2027 Grammys, Swift is set to appear at another awards show: the 2026 CMAs. Swift, who received a nomination for Single of the Year with “I Knew It, I Knew You,” confirmed her plans to attend the ceremony and perform. Prior to this, Swift had not performed at the CMAs for 13 years — which is her lucky number.

“Looks like I haven’t yee’d my last haw,” Swift wrote via her Instagram Stories after the nominations were announced. “See you there Nov 18.”

#3593. Andrew Scott On What Makes Elsinore “So Moving”

Although the emotional core of Elsinore is centered around beloved actor Ian Charleston dealing with terminal illness, its star Andrew Scott says the film has as much heart as it does humor.

“The most singular thing about our film I think is the humor in it,” he said during a panel conversation at the inaugural Vanity Fair Screening Room at LACMA on Friday. “The tragedy in some ways is a little bit like Hamlet itself, but you can't make a film about Ian Charleston without having gags in it. He was incredibly funny. Every person [who knew him] said he was just wickedly funny, and flirtatious, and he was always looking towards the light, and he had a certain degree of courage. So that is something I think that we all share as a sense of humor.”

Andrew Scott, Billie Piper, Stephen Beresford and Rebecca Ford at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026

Elsinore tells the story of Scottish actor Ian Charleson (Scott) who attempts to perform Hamlet at the National Theatre while secretly living with AIDS. Scott has received early acclaim for his powerful portrayal of Charleson. Before the film began Vanity Fair’s West Coast Editor John Ross warned the audience that "first you're going to laugh, then you're going to cry," while watching Scott’s performance.

“I think … why the film is so moving is because [Charleson’s] not wallowing at any point. He was insanely courageous,” continued Scott. “So that to me was the thing that we were the most

insistent on in some ways. And that's really all down to finding actors who in this extraordinary ensemble have a really terrific sense of humor. And we kind of knew that we could, with the screenplay, get the best actors in the country. And I feel we did.”

The panel conversation featured Scott, costar Billie Piper, and writer Stephen Beresford, moderated by VF's Senior Hollywood Correspondent Rebecca Ford, following an exclusive screening of the film.

Billie Piper at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026

For Piper, who plays Charleston's close friend Patsy, she relied heavily on Beresford's script for her prep, as well as information she gleaned from those who actually knew Patsy, and Charleston.

“I've spoken to a few members of the family, their friends, and then I sort of cherry-picked things from people I'd known in the beginning of my career, the louder figures in our industry,” she said. “And then I did my own interpretation and just had a good time. It's a very moving story, but I had a lot of fun playing that part. She's a really joyful character to play, I enjoyed the comedy. And I understand that a lot of her jokes are coming from a place of despair.”

Beresford, who has known Scott for 25 years, said he didn't initially think of his longtime friend for the role, but should have.

“The story of Ian, and Ian's Hamlet [performance] is legendary in the British theater,” he said. “So many people said it was the greatest Hamlet they'd ever seen, and that it had this incredible quality. So I knew about the story, and then it was brought to me actually as an idea by a producer who said, ‘What about writing about Ian Charleston, and what about Andrew playing Ian Charleston?’ And then I just thought, ‘Well, why didn't I have that idea myself five years ago?’ So yeah, that's really how it happened, and I started to research it, the details of the story were so incredible, and so moving.”

Stephen Beresford at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026.

Scott, who famously played Hamlet onstage 150 times beginning in 2017, prior to filming Elsinore, closed out the panel conversation by reciting his favorite line from the classic tragedy.

“When Hamlet says the line about the war that was going on—and this was written 400 years ago—it just seems so relevant to what he might have been experiencing at the time, which is: ‘I see the imminent death of 20,000 men who for a fantasy, a trick of fame, go to their graves like beds.’ The idea that that was written 400 years ago, and that he was watching 50 percent of his friends die for no reason and be neglected by governments, and derided by the public. And it was just happening, and happening time and time again.”

Scott continued: “The reason that I love it so much is that when I was doing Hamlet myself, of course I wasn't thinking about the AIDS crisis, but the enduring nature of art, something that was written 400 years ago by Shakespeare, could actually be of use to somebody in 1989 and then be reproduced again in 2026 and be of use. And that idea of art being useful down the lines is so moving to me.”

Vanity Fair's Global Editorial Director Mark Guiducci, Elsinore stars Andrew Scott and Billie Piper and writer Stephen Beresford at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026.

#3592. “Physical” GTA 6 Copies Might Be Vulnerable To A Very Stupid But Serious Trick

Grand Theft Auto 6 ditched traditional discs for its "physical" launch, with Rockstar's game being sold as a digital code-in-box at retailers beginning this week. However, it appears a packaging choice may have accidentally left the game vulnerable to thieves--assuming they have a flashlight.

As shared on the forum ResetEra, users who received a physical version of Grand Theft Auto 6, at least in PEGI regions, report that the game's download code is printed directly on the inside of the cover rather than on a card or separate insert. When a flashlight is focused on the cover from the outside of the closed game case, the download code is visible in reverse.

In other words, there's a serious risk people could go into a store, do this trick, redeem the code, and leave the poor soul who actually buys the game off the shelf without GTA 6.

At this time, the trick does not seem to work on North American copies of GTA 6, as the code is intentionally obscured. Why Rockstar would not use this strategy on all regions is unclear. We've reached out to Rockstar for an explanation and will update this post if and when we receive a response.

If you happen to get your GTA 6 code stolen after paying $80, you can at least sleep soundly knowing that the thief can't play the game yet. Code-in-box copies, as well as digital preorders, all unlock for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S on November 19.

#3590. GTA 6 Is Like The Olympics – “A Rare Cultural Moment” With Massive Ripple Effects

After years of development, multiple delays, and what can only be assumed to be one of the biggest production budgets ever, Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 launches on November 19. The game is poised to "blot out the sun," some experts believe, and its release looms so large that other gaming companies are shifting dates for their own games to stay out of the blast radius. 

Francis Lawrence, the director of the new Hunger Games movie Sunrise on the Reaping, which comes out a day after GTA 6, has said he hopes people can find the time to play the game and watch his movie. In short, GTA 6 is seen by some as a black hole that will suck up time, attention, and money from the broader gaming economy--and even workplaces, as people dive into the 80-hour game they've been waiting a decade to play. 

To help make sense of, and contextualize, the enormity of GTA 6's looming launch, GameSpot caught up with Bart Spiegel of the global professional services and research company PricewaterhouseCoopers, or PwC. He told GameSpot that GTA 6 is "something much bigger than a traditional entertainment launch," and is more akin to an event like the Olympics.

He believes GTA 6 is a "rare cultural moment" that "commands extraordinary attention and creates economic activity well beyond the event itself."

Spiegel said he foresees potential shifts beyond gaming, in places like TV viewership, music consumption, social media engagement, and even travel. "In an increasingly fragmented entertainment landscape, it's rare for a single release to command this much attention across so many industries simultaneously. That's what makes this moment so significant," he said.

An economics professor recently claimed that about 1.5 million people plan to "call out sick" to play GTA 6, and this could come at a "cost" of $1 billion to the US economy. Spiegel said people should remember that GTA 6 isn't anything new or special as it relates to taking time off work. "People regularly plan time off around major cultural and entertainment events, and this is another example of consumers prioritizing an experience they're excited about," he said.

That being said, Spiegel remarked that PwC has observed estimates suggesting time-off requests near GTA 6's release could be 9% to 17% higher than normal. "But what's more interesting to me is what happens outside the workplace. If millions of people are spending additional hours gaming, they're potentially spending less time watching television, going out to restaurants, or engaging in other activities," he said.

"And unlike a sporting event that lasts a few hours or a few weeks, this experience could keep people engaged for months. So the broader economic implications may extend well beyond a single day of missed work," he added.

"Huge net positive"

GTA 6 is expected to be an enormous success commercially--it's reportedly already sold 11 million units through pre-purchases, and that could rise to 25 million at launch. That would work out to $2 billion in revenue, which would cover the game's entire development budget and most of its marketing spend, Sensor Tower said. But many are also saying that GTA 6 represents the last of a dying breed, and that other publishers might learn all the wrong lessons from its success. Spiegel said GTA 6 is going to be a "huge net positive for the gaming industry as a whole," in part because its success will reiterate to the broader entertainment and media landscape that games are culturally significant. At the same time, Spiegel said he doesn't foresee a world in which other publishers try to replicate a blockbuster of this magnitude. 

"Very few organizations have the capital, expertise, and intellectual property required to support investments on this scale. These are extraordinary events, not necessarily repeatable business models," Spiegel said. 

If GTA 6 is the huge success it's projected to be, it could positively uplift the broader gaming ecosystem in a lot of ways, Spiegel continued. 

"It could attract new audiences, renew investor interest, and create opportunities across advertising, payments, technology, and content creation. The real lesson isn't that everyone needs to build the next billion-dollar game. It's that gaming is an increasingly powerful part of the entertainment economy, with opportunities that extend well beyond the games themselves," he said.

Some companies, like Ubisoft, see GTA 6 not as something to be strictly afraid of. CEO Yves Guillemot says, that's because the rising tide that is GTA 6 could help drive more people to gaming overall. In fact, Ubisoft is putting out a big new update for one of its biggest games, Rainbow Six Siege, right around GTA 6's launch.

Mat Piscatella of Circana reminded people that not everyone wants to play GTA 6, and he pushed back against the theory that it's a bad business idea to launch a game near GTA 6.

"The fear of many teams to put their game in the same window as GTA is completely overblown. GTA is going to be a massive game. Of course it is. It’s going to be a huge cultural event, but not every one of the 49 million people who own a PS5 or an Xbox Series in the US is going to be interested in that," he told GamesBeat.

Could GTA 6 lead the push to more in-game ads?

Spiegel went on to say that one additional follow-on effect from GTA 6 could be something that gamers might balk at but publishers and investors might salivate over. He said that if GTA 6 succeeds in the way people expect it to, and draw people into its world for tens--or even hundreds--of hours, that could demonstrate to the wider market that it's time for gaming, as an industry, to do more with advertising. 

"When millions of people are spending substantial amounts of time in interactive entertainment environments, it's natural for advertisers and investors to consider how they might participate," he said. 

Advertising for mobile and social games is already commonplace, but it's less present in the PC and console gaming market. There are examples, of course, as companies have already undertaken efforts to put ads into gaming with mixed results. Gamers quickly revolted when EA put ads in a UFC game, prompting EA to pull them quickly to help quell the backlash. Despite that, EA recently announced the formation of a new EA Advertising division that will seek to put ads "directly into gameplay." That announcement didn't go over well, either, as fans pushed back against the idea of having to see ads in yet another place in their life. Other examples have been received more positively, or at least ambivalently, with a trucking company buying ad space in the American Truck Simulator series to help recruit staff. 

Xbox, for its part, has big plans to put more ads in gaming. Xbox CSO Matthew Ball said advertising in console games could help with the "two-sided problem" that AAA gaming faces today. Development costs keep going up and up, and Ball said ads--as long as they're not overly in-your-face--could be a way to help developers make more money and solidify their business fundamentals. Of course, if these companies insert more ads into gaming, that doesn't mean they'll stop hawking things like DLC, microtransactions, and battle passes; they'll likely both happen in concert. As Spiegel sees it, though, if executed correctly, advertising could be a big boon for gaming.

"What's particularly interesting is that the opportunity extends beyond placing advertisements inside games. There's an entire ecosystem of digital advertising infrastructure, technology, and services that could benefit as gaming continues to grow. I expect we'll see increasing interest in those opportunities, particularly from investors looking for exposure to gaming without taking on the considerable financial risks associated with developing blockbuster titles," he said.

More investment

During the COVID years, the gaming industry saw massive revenue and player growth as people, forced to stay inside due to stay-at-home orders, turned to games to pass the time, have fun, and connect with friends. At the same time, interest rates were historically low. The cost to borrow money was so attractive that publishers ramped up significantly. 

The COVID-era boost to gaming did not last, though, and the industry is now challenged, to say the least, with numerous developers cutting staff, cancelling projects, and scaling back in other ways. If GTA 6 is indeed a massive success, it could trigger renewed interest in gaming as an investment vehicle, Spiegel believes, but not necessarily exclusively for funding new games and studios. Instead, Spiegel said he foresees big investment growth for discrete elements of gaming, including advertising, payment services, and AI buildouts.

"I absolutely think a release of this magnitude will get the attention of investors, corporate executives, and private equity firms. But I don't necessarily think that translates into another wave of billion-dollar game development," he said. "The economics of producing games at this scale are incredibly challenging, and very few organizations have the resources, expertise, and intellectual property necessary to justify those investments."

"Instead, I think investors will increasingly ask how they can participate in the broader gaming ecosystem," Spiegel added. "That could mean opportunities in advertising, payment infrastructure, technology services, mobile gaming, or artificial intelligence applications that support game development."

On the subject of AI, Spiegel said he believes it's a "particularly interesting variable" because it could, at least in theory, allow developers to work more efficiently and bring down costs. There is debate about whether or not this is a genuine reality or wishful thinking on the part of AI companies trying to sell their products and services. Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick, for example, recently told Business Insider that, despite Take-Two adopting AI products for some of its workflows, the company has not seen a material decrease in its cost structure. In fact, many theorize that AI-supported workflows will only make work more intense. For his part, Spiegel said AI in game development remains only an "emerging opportunity rather than a guaranteed outcome."

"The longer-term impact may be less about creating another generation of massive blockbusters and more about directing investment toward the businesses and technologies that support the gaming economy," he said. 

Who should be afraid?

A lot has already been said and written about publishers moving their release dates to avoid GTA 6, and Spiegel said he foresees dramatic possibilities for how GTA 6 could take the wind out of the sails of other entertainment near its launch. He said GTA 6 is not just a major gaming launch. Instead, he thinks it's an "event that could temporarily reshape how millions of consumers spend their time and money."

"Streaming could be particularly vulnerable. Every hour someone spends gaming is potentially an hour they're not watching a television show or movie. And because this launch falls just before the holiday season, it could make it difficult for streaming services to match the exceptionally strong viewership numbers we saw last year," he said.

Movie theaters could be tested, Spiegel said, and one highly anticipated film, The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, will be one to watch in particular. It comes to theaters on Friday, November 20, which is one day after GTA 6 releases. Director Francis Lawrence said he hopes fans find the time to play GTA 6 and go see his movie, but it remains to be seen what effect, if any, GTA 6's release will have on that film's performance at the box office. Spiegel said movie studios are banking on the belief that the theatrical experience "offers something consumers can't get from their living rooms." 

There is a Thursday Night Football game happening on the same day that GTA 6 releases, with the Indianapolis Colts taking on the Houston Texans. Spiegel said the live-sports category overall could be "more resilient" because of its nature as an event happening live that fans of those teams, or fans of the NFL in general, feel compelled to watch live as it happens. A movie or TV show, meanwhile, is on-demand entertainment. 

GTA 6 is a hugely anticipated release, and it's poised to bring lapsed gamers back into the fold, but anyone who doesn't already have a PS5 or Xbox Series X|S should prepare themselves for sticker shock. That's because, for a variety of reasons, new consoles today are actually hundreds of dollars more expensive than they were when they launched in 2020.

Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick has frankly acknowledged, "The rising cost of hardware is not a good thing." At the same time, Zelnick isn't shaking in his boots about what this means for GTA 6. He thinks GTA 6 will be so good and so compelling that people will buy in no matter what.

"I don’t think it will slow us down any because, you know, we’re delivering, we believe we’re delivering experiences that people want,” Zelnick said. “However, a lower price point for hardware would be a good thing because there’d be more hardware in people’s hands."

Who benefits?

In terms of companies, products, people, and services that could benefit from the ripple effects of GTA 6's release, Spiegel said music associated with the game could surge in listening activity. This has already happened, as streams of Tom Petty's "Love Is A Long Road" surged after the first trailer for GTA 6 used the song back in 2023. More recently, Cliff Richard's 1976 hit "Devil Woman" showed up in the GTA 6 Extended Look on Netflix, helping the song reach more people, including young people who maybe never even knew about the song. Spiegel said social media platforms could benefit from GTA 6's release as well, thanks to fans uploading gameplay clips, livestreams, and other forms of user-generated content inspired by GTA 6. Beyond this, the world of food delivery could see an uptick in activity as people opt to stay in to play GTA 6 (while in-person restaurants and other nightlife venues could take a hit). 

"The broader point is that the impact could extend into parts of the economy we don't traditionally associate with gaming," Spiegel said. "For business leaders, the question is whether they're competing with this cultural moment for consumer attention or finding ways to participate in it. That's what makes this launch so much more interesting than simply tracking how many copies are sold."

#3589. Dan Campbell Issues Update on Aidan Hutchinson Following Celebration Injury

Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell discussed a shocking injury to star defensive end Aidan Hutchinson, which came during a sack celebration on Sunday, November 16.

“We’ll know more when we get back in the States,” Campbell, 50, told reporters after the Lions’ 35-10 victory over the New England Patriots in Munich, Germany, on Sunday. “Anytime you lose a player of his caliber, the type of teammate he is — he’s a captain of ours — that doesn’t make things easy. But I thought guys stepped up in his wake and showed up for us today.”

Hutchinson, 26, injured himself during the first quarter on Sunday after he jumped in the air to celebrate a sack of Patriots quarterback Drake Maye.

Maye, 24, was also hurt on the play and missed the rest of the game. ESPN reported on Monday, November 16, that Maye will miss “an extended period, and possibly the remainder of the season.”

While the Lions have not confirmed Hutchinson’s injury status, ESPN reported on Monday that he tore the ACL in his right knee and will miss the rest of the season.

Hutchinson received an initial MRI in Germany before returning home with the team on Sunday. He is expected to undergo further testing in the coming days.

The injury on Sunday is the latest in a string of unfortunate incidents for Hutchinson. In 2024, he broke the tibia and fibula in his left leg in Week 6 against the Dallas Cowboys, forcing him to miss the rest of the season, including the Lions’ playoff loss to the Washington Commanders.

Hutchinson also underwent surgery for a fracture in his right ankle suffered during his junior season at the University of Michigan.

The Lions (7-2) are currently tied for first place in the NFC North with the Minnesota Vikings and Chicago Bears. Detroit returns to action on Sunday, November 22, when they host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Hutchinson’s devastating injury comes just weeks after the Lions lost fellow defensive stalwart Jack Campbell.

Jack, 26, remains hospitalized after suffering a neck injury against the Vikings on November 1. The linebacker broke his silence about the incident in a statement released by the Lions on November 4.

“My family and I want to sincerely thank everyone for the overwhelming amount of love, prayers, and support we’ve received over the past few days,” Jack said. “It means more to us than words can express.”

He added, “I’m incredibly encouraged by the progress I’ve made in such a short period of time,” he announced. “I have full movement in my lower body, and I’m continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body. I know there’s still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic. I’m taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better.”

#3588. Xbox Project Helix Is A Console That Plays PC Games, Not The Other Way Around

Xbox has revealed more details about its next-gen device, Project Helix, describing it as a "console capable of playing games from your PC."

Prominently featured in the Xbox 25th Anniversary Magazine, VP of next-gen Jason Ronald said the Xbox Series X|S successor is designed to build on the successes — and hard lessons — of previous Xbox generations, with fewer barriers to play.  "When we think about Project Helix, it's really designed to be the ultimate gaming machine--one that removes all the barriers of play that have historically existed," Ronald said. "My entire library is accessible to me. I'm able to bring four generations of my Xbox library and progression with me and have it available instantly. And we remove the arbitrary constraints between console and PC games."

Ronald added that the Project Helix family of devices isn't purely focused on traditional next-gen themes like better graphics, but on thinking ahead to create "innovative" experiences. "We don't think the next generation is defined by 8K, or 240 hertz, or some of the traditional metrics--it's really about gameplay innovation," Ronald explained. "We're very clear on the design goal: Helix is designed to be a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC. It is not a PC that can also play console games. The goal is making it easy, intuitive, and instant to access my games. But if you're a hardcore gamer or a power user who wants to have that deeper level of customizability across settings and performance options, you can absolutely go do it."

Project Helix will also let "hardcore" gamers customize their gaming experience, but how much will all of this cost? Xbox isn't revealing a ballpark figure for Project Helix yet, but Ronald did mention the company is aiming to balance state-of-the-art gaming with an "affordable" price tag. Game preservation will also play a key role, letting users bring their Xbox library with them, and Ronald teased Project Helix as a brand that spans multiple facets of gaming, from living room experiences to handheld sessions and cloud streaming. As a sign of things to come, the Xbox mode on the recently released ROG Xbox Ally was mentioned as the direction the gaming division is headed.

The news on Project Helix comes at a time when Xbox has had several highs and lows throughout 2026. This year saw several first-party games release and earn plenty of acclaim, while the anniversary celebrations included a special-edition Xbox Series X that few people could get their hands on — for retail price, that is. At the same time, the rise of Asha Sharma as Xbox CEO has seen scores of jobs and studios slashed from the Xbox family as the company undergoes a "reset" aimed at making it more profitable.

#3587. Hillary Clinton Showed Up For Dinner at Gloria Steinem’s Townhouse

It’s a dark and stormy November night at Gloria Steinem’s townhouse, and Hillary Clinton has something to say about the 2026 election. “One of my most anticipated moments will be watching Donald Trump walk into the State of the Union through the now more than one hundred women members of the House of Representatives. I just want them all to stare at him and say, ‘You fired us from jobs we were qualified for. You insulted us. You demeaned our ambition. You undermined our place in government and society. And we’re here.’”

Huma Abedin, Busy Philips, and Paloma Elsesser.

The former Secretary of State and 2016 presidential candidate is a last-minute but highly anticipated arrival to this dinner honoring Steinem, the late activist. She passed away in September, but the feminist pathfinder was known for throwing these salon-type events (she called them “circles”) at her Upper East Side townhouse, which she bought for just $30,000 in the late ’60s. It’s overflowing with books (I spy Marilyn by Norman Mailer, Jane Fonda’s War by Mary Hershberger, and several Eleanor Roosevelt biographies on the shelves), pictures (there’s one framed of Steinem alongside Mariska Hargitay) and Indian art. (Steinem spent two formative years in the country.) There are magnets in her kitchen of Wonder Woman, Frida Kahlo, and a cloth finger puppet of Hillary Clinton. A political button is pinned to it that says “Another Bitch for Hillary.” The whole place smells like a Cire Trudon candle, and everyone’s drinking negronis. (Which actually isn’t technically very Steinem—her favorite cocktail was a margarita—but the negronis go with the night’s dinner, prepared by Lilia chef Missy Robbins.) Yet this is one of the first events at the townhouse that Steinem herself isn’t here to lead.

Jihae, Lux Pascal, Naomi Watts, and Bethann Hardison.

Amy Richards, a feminist activist whom many consider to be the daughter Steinem never had—a title Richards rejects because her mentor “didn’t want kids”—stood up at one point to tell the crowd that this is what Steinem would have wanted. Growing up with a transient father and a mentally volatile mother, the late activist took near-obsessive care in maintaining a welcoming home she could share with others. “As long as I knew Gloria, she always said, ‘I just want my home to be the way it’s always been.’ She wanted it to be filled with people,” Richards says. “She didn’t grow up with a home. She was traveling the country for the first 10 years of her life and then lived with her mother, who was not very stable.”

At least Steinem’s still here on the wall: Months before her death, she posed for a series of portraits by Paola Kudacki for Weldun, a platform that offers physically adaptive and functional fashion. It was a bit of a small miracle that Steinem said yes. “I will say, Gloria did not always love to be photographed,” Richards says. “Especially in her later years—not because of wrinkles or aging, but she was just like, ‘Aren’t there enough pictures of me?’” Weldun and the Gloria Steinem Foundation are presenting tonight’s dinner, and mementos of Steinem are everywhere. On the fireplace mantle sits a pair of her signature Ray-Ban aviators. But Gloria’s stuff isn’t the same as Gloria herself.

Former secretary of state Hillary Clinton hugging Melissa McCarthy.

Which is probably why, in a crowd of women that include Huma Abedin, Mariska Hargitay, Padma Lakshmi, Melissa McCarthy, and Bethann Hardison—who, at the ripe age of 84, shows up wearing Gucci—Clinton’s unexpected arrival feels seismic, like Gloria sent someone in her place. (Hardison tells me she thinks Steinem used whatever divine power she’s got up there to launch the Blue Wave: “She’s probably saying she helped it happen!”) Whatever your views on Clinton’s politics, she was the first woman to receive a presidential nomination from a major party. Paloma Elsesser and I sit crouched in a corner of the room, glued to the window. “There’s mother,” the supermodel whispers to me as Clinton exits her car into the pouring rain and walks up to the townhouse door.

Guests at dinner honoring the late Gloria Steinem.

“Hi, everybody,” Clinton says as she walks in. The entire dinner comes to a silent halt. “Hi,” the room responds in unison. Madame Secretary doesn’t seem to like the fuss, probably because 30 or so people intensely staring at you when you arrive at a party is objectively unsettling. “Go back to eating!” she says, motioning to the Missy Robbins meal on the table. Clinton sits down next to Naomi Watts and warmly greets Busy Philips, who stumped for Clinton back in 2016. Hargitay blows her a kiss across the table. All anyone wants to do is talk to Clinton about the 2026 election, in which Democrats won at least 55 seats in the Senate and 256 in the House to take both majorities in the US Congress. At the end of the meal—and after a proper catch-up with Shonda Rhimes—Clinton tries to leave, but she can’t. Guests block the door, clamoring to chat her up.

Amid the Clinton traffic jam, I ask Hargitay about the photo. She can’t remember exactly what it is from. “Was it Bravo? Was it with Andy…what’s his name?” But she can guess what she thinks Steinem might say about the blue wave: “There is a God!”

I watch Clinton finally make her exit. It’s late, so I wait several minutes before I descend the stairs to leave too. (I wait for Elsesser, Watts, Hardinn, and Lux Pascal to finish taking a selfie on the steps.) But I spoke too soon: Clinton’s stuck waiting for the coat check, another group of women crowded around her hoping to say something—or, more likely, hoping she says something. With the way this night is going, Clinton might be the last one at the party.

#3586. Lindsay Clancy Will Be Retried in Murder Case, New Trial Date Scheduled

Lindsay Clancy will be retried in her murder case, with Judge William Sullivan declaring that her new trial will begin on March 29, 2027.

Clancy, 36, appeared in Plymouth Superior Court on Monday, November 16, to discuss the future of her case after her mistrial in September. During the latest hearing, prosecutors shared their plans to retry Clancy, according to CBS News.

After the commonwealth argued that the retrial should begin in May, Sullivan, 69, pushed for a March date. (Sullivan previously announced his plans to retire in 2027.)

Sullivan has made several rulings regarding the case since the last hearing on November 9, in which he denied Clancy’s motion to dismiss the murder charges.

Plymouth County District Attorney Tim Cruz has the final say in retrying Clancy on first-degree murder charges and has the power to try Clancy on a lesser charge, such as second-degree murder or manslaughter.

Clancy was previously charged with murder in connection to the deaths of her kids, Cora, 5, Dawson, 3, and Callan, 8 months, in January 2023.

She never denied killing her kids, but her defense argued that she should not be held criminally responsible because she was suffering from postpartum psychosis at the time of the deaths. Meanwhile, the prosecution argued that she was aware of what she was doing and that her suicide attempt after the murders indicated the killings were intentional.

The jury deliberated for seven days until Sullivan declared a mistrial on September 4 when the jury said they could not come to a unanimous verdict. Eleven of the jurors voted to find Clancy not guilty by reason of insanity, while holdout juror Michael P. Desronvil stood firm that she was guilty.

Desronvil has maintained his beliefs that Clancy was guilty, previously breaking his silence while speaking to Fox News on September 28.

“I know the whole focus has been on me, but we want to reel the whole thing back and put the focus on the three angels [Clancy’s three children],” he said at the time. “[They] are the ones who can’t speak for themselves. The ones that can’t defend themselves. The ones that can’t fight their own battles.”

Desronvil continued, “I want to thank God for my Catholic faith. I want to thank God for giving me the ability to love my daughter. Foremost, I would like to thank everyone — every individual — that has supported me throughout this difficult situation. Your prayers, your emotional support, your psychological support is tremendous [for] my heart.”

#3584. I tested the Halliday G2 AI smart glasses and they turned me into a walking 'cheat sheet' — but everyone could tell

Keep exploring and earning more as a member.

Unlock and manage exclusive Tom’s Guide member rewards.

Join the Tom's Guide Club for quick access. Enter your email below and we'll send confirmation, and sign you up to our newsletter.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The Halliday G2 AI smart glasses are a step in the right direction, delivering camera-less specs with helpful AI features in a comfortable yet chunky (and dorky) design. But these smart glasses offer a near-identical experience to their rivals, all while not quite hitting the mark. While its bright dual micro-LED projectors offer clear views of helpful features, it's let down by subpar open-ear audio and tools that aren't quite as intuitive to use.

Why you can trust Tom's Guide Our writers and editors spend hours analyzing and reviewing products, services, and apps to help find what's best for you. Find out more about how we test, analyze, and rate.

When I first heard of Halliday making a splash back at CES 2025 by putting an "invisible" built-in display into its smart glasses, I was amazed by what the future of smart specs holds. Now, the company has refined its AI smart glasses in the Halliday G2, but this time, it isn't quite as revolutionary.

With its dual micro LED engines and waveguide optics on both lenses to deliver a simplistic green dot matrix style text, an open-ear audio system for personal sound and a bundle of features utilizing a Halliday AI assistant, the Halliday G2 AI smart glasses are a subtle pair of specs made for seamless daily wear. Well, I say "subtle" loosely, as everyone will know that you're wearing smart glasses with these on. And wait, many of these features sound a little too familiar...

These aren't just taking cues from the Even Realities G2, as the Halliday G2 offers like-for-like features in the exact same waveguide display format. I mean, it's even called "G2," for pete's sake! From the Meeting Flow feature that can summarize, research and transcribe conversations in meetings, which is just the Even Realities G2's Conversate feature, to the Cheat Sheet feature that acts as a teleprompter, which is just Teleprompt on the Even Realities G2, there's not a lot here to pick these over its clear inspiration.

But that's not to say its features aren't handy to use, especially when it comes to its Halliday AI, which is snappy at answering whatever you ask. Along with its informative dashboard (such as displaying the time, weather and more), notifications that are clear to read and its helpful Translate feature, there are day-to-day benefits of wearing the Halliday G2s. That said, it's still held back by other annoyances, like a subpar open-ear audio system and a Stealth Mode that doesn't do a good job at being "stealthy."

But are these the best smart glasses for you? After wearing the Halliday G2 daily, here are my thoughts.

Dual micro-LED, 600 x 300 per-eye resolution, 1,600 nits peak brightness

The Halliday G2s have clearly come a long way from their first iteration, making for a commendable pair of AI smart glasses that focus on everyday wear with helpful features, rather than "pervy glasses" with a camera in them.

When first seeing the Halliday G2, I made an all-too-quick assumption that these would give my head and ears a tough time. These are thick, blocky specs, and I could almost see how much they weigh from the look of them. But I was wrong.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Coming in at just 1.7 ounces, the Hallifay G2s are actually one of the more comfortable AI glasses I've worn. The magnesium alloy frame keeps the weight off, but the glasses themselves have a good distribution of weight with the tech that is housed in their temples.

Not quite as light or slim as the Even Realities G2 (1.2 ounces), but around a similar size and weight to the Ray-Ban Meta (Gen 2) at around 1.79 ounces.

While I wouldn't say these feel premium to the touch, especially for the price, I would have these smart specs sitting on my face all day without being irritated by sore ears or frame imprints on my nose or around my eyes.

Most of its tech, from the 210 mAh battery to the open-ear audio it boasts, is housed in the thick temples (also like the Ray-Ban Meta specs). This makes them naturally thick, but this works out, as it makes gesture control along the right temple easier to manage. That includes tapping and swiping to navigate around in-display menus and features.

It takes a little while to get the hang of, but it works like a charm once it clicks, and the bar-like temples make it easy to swipe and slide a finger along.

You'll also find a Halliday G2 hard case, and it's sturdy, stylish and sizeable enough to easily slip in the G2s and close its strong magnetic clasp. It's no Even Realities G2 smart case that charges the glasses, but it does a fine job of keeping the Halliday G2s protected.

This is one of the first signs of similarities between the Halliday G2 and Even Realities G2. But this is a nice trait to share, because it's wonderful to have a discreet display that blends into the real world as an overlay that's easy to see and read.

Using dual micro-LED engines to cover both lenses, the Halliday G2s feature binocular waveguide displays for a minimal, yet extremely helpful, dashboard right in front of your eyes.

As with the Even Realities G2, the display is made up of green dot-matrix-style text, akin to the Pip-Boy from "Fallout." It's not obtrusive, and it makes it easy to glance at while going about your day. It helps that the waveguides have a 600 x 300 per-eye resolution and a whopping 1,600 nits of peak brightness. And yes, that means I could clearly see the display even during bright days (those are now limited in the U.K.).

Whether it's notifications coming in via your smartphone or the dashboard displaying the weather forecast for the next few hours, text is clear, bright and sharp, yet doesn't overtake your full real-world view, either. This is the kind of simplistic, futuristic display I've come to enjoy in smart glasses, so keep on this path, Halliday!

Having a personal HUD to show you the time, date, weather forecast and more at a glance is already a nice perk, but using the Halliday G2 to summarize conversations, translate languages in real time, give you instant answers just by asking it and view text via a teleprompter is what makes these glasses actually "smart."

The Halliday G2's key features include Meeting Flow, where live AI agents manage whole conversations (geared towards business meetings) by tracking, summarizing, transcribing and quickly researching what is said; Cheatsheet, a teleprompter that's (sort of) invisible to everyone but you, with customizable read speeds; and Translation, which can translate conversations in real time for over 45 different languages.

Meeting Flow is the star of the show, and it did a great job of getting all the key points said in one of my daily stand-up meetings and organizing this into different sections, such as having a To-Do List and a Quick Summary of everything that was said. I also quite liked the Thread Tracker, which helps you get back on topic before the conversation goes off the rails (which is a fun problem I generally have in meetings).

Now, there are plenty of AI agents that do this automatically in virtual meetings, like Google Gemini, Otter AI and plenty more. But the Halliday G2s give you a personal meeting assistant right in your view during meetings, which can be helpful to many.

Cheatsheet and Translate are also snappy in action, and I was impressed with the Halliday AI assistant being able to answer random questions on the fly. For example, while I was watching the cult classic "Twin Peaks," I asked where it was generally filmed, and it was quick to answer (it's in Snoqualmie Valley near Seattle).

Do any of these features sound familiar? They should, as you'll find all these Halliday G2 features on the Even Realities G2 — just named differently. For example, Conversate on the Even Realities is just Meeting Flow here, while Teleprompt is Cheat Sheet and Translate is... Translate.

While these features are like-for-like, that doesn't make Halliday's tools any less helpful, as they still do what they set out to do well.

Unless you're looking for thick, Spongebob-like glasses, the Halliday G2s aren't the most seamless smart glasses you can get, and they have far too much in common with the Even Realities G2, but with a couple more downsides, to stand out.

I can almost hear Homer Simpson shouting "Neeerd!" out of his car when I put on the Halliday G2s, and that alone makes me avoid wearing these in public.

The G2s are clearly smart glasses, as everyone I came across had pointed out at first glance. That's not such a terrible thing, but it's just how thick and bulky the smart specs are that makes them unappealing. Of course, glasses come in all shapes and sizes, and some frame styles are better suited to others. Some may enjoy the bulkiness, but there is a limit to frames being too thick, too.

Along with this, it's a shame there is only one style of the Halliday G2s, unlike the many different frames of the Ray-Ban Meta lineup and the couple of options the Even Realities G2 offers.

While the waveguide displays are discreet, others can still see the green light from the lenses at certain angles. That's why the Halliday G2 smart glasses have a Stealth Mode, so you can subtly read incoming messages or AI conversations without that green hue people may be able to see.

Or, that's what it wants to do anyway. In reality, it simply dims the green text on the waveguide displays, but it's still able to be seen at different angles (as my friends have confirmed). It's not as noticeable when Stealth Mode is turned off, but I wouldn't exactly call this stealthy.

At the very least, Stealth Mode on the Halliday G2s aren't as creepy as smart glasses with cameras, seeing as it's just text.

The only major difference between the Halliday G2 and Even Realities G2 is that the former comes with an open-ear audio system, much like the Ray-Ban Meta glasses. You can hear phone calls, listen to music or podcasts and hear a very annoying clicking sound with each action you do.

I'd prefer to not have any audio in smart glasses aimed at being everyday specs for the usual glasses wearer, especially when sound easily leaks out for everyone to hear what you're listening to, and it sounds more hollow than anything else. I also imagine the G2's battery takes a hit from this, being just around 12 hours before needing a charge. Not bad, but the Even Realities G2 can last a couple of days before needing a boost.

I understand that it's trying to be the all-in-one system for your face, so you no longer need one of the best earbuds, but it's far from accomplishing that task. And yes, I turned off that navigation click as soon as I heard it, which also meant turning off the ringtone.

The Halliday G2 are the type of AI smart glasses that I'm a fan of, offering a comfortable fit for all-day wear with helpful AI features that are intuitive to use and snappy in action. Being able to check the time or weather on the fly without having to take out your phone, summarize conversations with key talking points and translate other languages are huge perks to have sitting on your face.

But the Halliday G2s succumb to the usual problem with smart glasses: they look too "smart." That's fine if big, chunky frames suit your style, but when the Even Realities G2 does it all better at the same retail price, but in a more casual design, then it's harder to recommend these over its competition.

While the Halliday G2 AI smart glasses are a step in the right direction, there are still a few features and design choices that the best smart glasses we recommend do better.

Follow Tom's Guide on Google News and add us as a preferred source to get our up-to-date news, analysis, and reviews in your feeds.

#3583. GTA 6 Nearing 15 Million Copies Sold And $1.5 Billion In Revenue, And The Game Isn’t Even Out Yet

The video game research company Sensor Tower has updated its GTA 6 sales tracker to reveal the latest, albeit unofficial, sales data for the open-world crime game. According to Sensor Tower, GTA 6 has now sold 14.94 million total units via pre-purchases, which works out to about $1.45 billion in gross revenue.

The report said PS5 sales are dominating the mix, with GTA 6 selling 11.13 million units on PS5 so far, compared to 3.81 million on Xbox Series X|S. That means of the 14.94 million GTA 6 sales so far, 74% are on PS5 and 26% on Xbox Series X|S.

In total, GTA 6 sales for PS5 have so far reached $1.08 billion in revenue, compared to $3.81 million for Xbox Series X|S. Sony and Microsoft keep about 30% of revenue due to their platform fees, so GTA 6 being a huge success directly benefits both of those companies.

The huge gap in sales between platforms is not surprising because the PS5 is dominating Xbox Series X|S in terms of console sales. In fact, GTA 6 is breaking records on Xbox, Microsoft has said, and the sales numbers for GTA 6 on Xbox line up with Xbox's share of the console market.

Sensor Tower is projecting as many as 25 million total pre-purchases for GTA 6 by launch, and if the 75/25 split holds, that would be about 18.5 million units on PS5 and 6.5 million on Xbox Series X|S.

GTA 6 is the most preordered game of all time for PlayStation and Xbox. If the 10 million pre-purchase number is real, that would break a record for most preorders set by Cyberpunk 2077 (8 million).

Sony holds the marketing rights for GTA 6 on PS5, but that doesn't mean that Microsoft is doing nothing to try to promote the game. Just recently, Microsoft announced a GTA 6-inspired custom Xbox console that sits inside an alligator.

Circana has released new data that shows that GTA 6 holds 29% purchase intent among US console and PC gamers. That means nearly 1 in 3 console and PC gamers in the US plan to buy GTA 6–this is the highest purchase intent that Circana has ever measured for any game.

GTA 6 may indeed be a gigantic hit commercially, and one that helps lift the entire industry with increased sales of hardware and accessories. But anyone looking to buy a new console to play GTA 6 is set for major sticker shock, as consoles today are more expensive than ever. Not only that, but GTA 6 is not going to save the industry’s many serious and deep-rooted issues, experts believe.

GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. The game's file size is about 212GB, and thankfully, preloading is already underway. The game unlocks on November 19 at midnight local time, and that means US players will be among the last in the world to get in.

People in New Zealand, meanwhile, will be the first in the world to play GTA 6. If you're thinking about booking a flight to the land of Hobbits, here are some tips for packing your PS5 safely.

#3581. Xbox Is Looking For Smarter Ways To Stop Its Next Console From Costing A Fortune

No one knows yet exactly what the next-gen Xbox console, Project Helix, will be, but most people are convinced it won't be cheap. The ongoing memory shortage has driven current-gen console prices skyward since 2024, with the Xbox Series X rising from $500 in 2020 to $800 in 2026. Project Helix is projected to cost as much as $1,800 at launch, but Microsoft aims to keep the price down when it eventually releases the device.

According to VP of next-gen Jason Ronald, techniques like neural rendering could help manage costs. "It's definitely a challenging time, but as a system and a platform designer, it's also one of the most exciting times, because we have to invent entirely new technology to continue to advance the state-of-the-art while also continuing to make things accessible and affordable," Ronald said in the Xbox 25th Anniversary Magazine. "This is a big reason why we're really focused on advancements like neural rendering, because it's an entirely new way to generate a frame without requiring more computational horsepower, additional memory, and things like that. I think you're going to see more innovation over the next three to five years than you've seen in the last 10 years."

In a nutshell, neural rendering uses AI to predict and generate high-quality video game frames while using only a portion of hardware power, similar to upscaling technoligies like PSSR, DLSS, and FSR. This could enable next-generation visual leaps while keeping the console accessible and reasonably priced for consumers. The other benefit is that the AI software models can improve over time through updates, as console hardware remains fixed over its lifespan, hence Ronald's quote about improvements reaching Project Helix over a few years into its run.

It remains to be seen how these breakthroughs will be spread across Project Helix, which Ronald teased as a family of devices that can address home, mobile, and cloud gaming needs. Xbox suggesting that it's working smarter to deliver an affordable gaming experience is an idea that Shawn Layden touched on recently, as the former PlayStation boss spoke about how Sony should be less concerned with chasing improved graphics and rather focus on making a cheaper PS5-level console instead.

Meanwhile, Sony is squeezing more life out of the PS5 generation with AI-guided upscaling technology, and the base model PS5 got its own version of this in the form of Quick Spectral Super Resolution. Originally available for only two games, QSSR is coming to more titles in the future, like Control Resonant, Arc Raiders, and No Man's Sky.

We've gotten glimpses of Lithgow in the role of the Hogwarts Headmaster in previously released Harry Potter footage, but this new clip puts more emphasis on his mannerisms and I am loving it.

The clip opens with the newly sorted first years seated with the rest of their houses and chanting for Dumbledore. Once they're tucking into their feast, Dumbledore and Professor McGonagall have a chat about Harry being sorted into Gryffindor. "The cat that got the cream" is a clever idiom from the headmaster, when taking into account McGonagall's animagus abilities. For such a brief conversation, it really tells us a lot about the headmaster. He's playful and thoughtful all at once.

When Minerva comments on how much Harry looks like his father, Dumbledore's response is:

Looks can be deceiving, Minerva. His nature is entirely his own.

I love that Dumbledore isn't quick to assume Harry is everything like his father. McGonagall's tone is affectionate of course, but still softly suggests some expectation from the 11-year-old that Dumbledore seems quick to gently shut down. There are so many sides to Albus Dumbledore, and I love how this clip shows Lithgow grasping more than one of them.

Beyond Lithgow's words in this scene, there's also his mannerisms. Before he sits down, Dumbledore snaps his fingers to prompt the food to appear on the tables. Then, when it's time for dessert, I'm assuming that little flourish of his fork as he's about to grab some meat, is the prompt to turn dinner service into dessert for the kids. It's little details like that that I can't wait to see more of.

On the less positive side, I'm not entirely sure I love the way the food appeared. There was something slightly off -- or maybe slightly too perfect? -- about the way the food snapped into reality that bugged me. I'm trying to keep an open mind as we see more magic in use in this series, and it's possible my brain is just too familiar with the sight of the plates appearing in the movie -- which is admittedly a wide shot from very far away before we see the food close up -- to accept this new version quite yet. (Considering some of the food featured in the movie had apparently spoiled after sitting out for days of filming, maybe I shouldn't cling so much to memories that scene.)

I will say that when the dessert appeared, my brain flashed back to that scene in Hook when Peter finally sees all the food at the table. Dumbledore may have conjured dessert for the students, but he conjured instant childhood memories over here, and my stomach growled.

We're a little more than a month out from the premiere of Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone. It seems likely that HBO will give us another glimpse or two between now and then, but nothing will compare to sitting down for the first episode when it debuts on Christmas. Between what we know and love from the books and scenes that weren't straight from the page, there will be a lot to dive into as Season 1 gets going.

#3579. GTA 6 Promo At KFC Is A Fake Funeral So You Can Take The Day Off To Play

The popular fried chicken chain KFC has announced a frankly absurd GTA 6 promotion: a fake funeral so people have a “legitimate” excuse to take the day off to play Rockstar’s latest.

The fake funeral for a woman, "Ann Alibi," will take place Thursday, November 19 at 11 AM at KFC Robina in Queensland. People can attend in person or watch the funeral by livestream. The local restaurant is part of a region of Australia known as the Gold Coast, which KFC says is the equivalent of GTA 6's Vice City (which itself is a stand-in for Miami).

"The service will include a hearse, coffin, floral tributes, a book of condolences, an order of service and even a heartfelt eulogy delivered by a surprise guest. All the appropriate arrangements for a fitting farewell," KFC said.

The restaurant is also handing out free fried chicken to anyone who shows up in person. For those who can't make the services, KFC will offer free delivery through its app across Australia on November 19.

Anyone planning to eat fried food and play video games should be mindful of what might happen to their controller ... unless you got your hands on the limited-edition "greaseproof" controller that Microsoft put out years ago. Check out the video below to see how an Xbox controller holds up to heavy grease.

A KFC spokesperson said of the GTA 6 promo, "We appreciate that Australians have responsibilities, but some occasions are simply too important to miss. And in accordance with Ann's final wishes, we've made sure the funeral takes place during working hours."

GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. People in Australia will be among the first in the world to play it since the game unlocks at midnight local time and not simultaneously around the world. This means people in the US will be among the last in the world to get to play GTA 6.

#3578. We Got A Grand Theft At Disney World Before GTA 6

The "We got X before GTA 6" meme continues as a Grand Theft has been reported at Walt Disney World's Epcot theme park just days before Rockstar's open-world crime game releases, and the meme comes to an end.

The Walt Disney World: Active Calls account, which tracks police reports in the Disney World area, said a Grand Theft call at Epcot came in at 9:52 PM on November 14.

There are no further details to go on here, but Grand Theft, known as Grand Larceny in some states, involves stealing something valuable. Epcot and Disney in general has lots of items that would be considered valuable.

This is the closest that Disney World might come to GTA 6, as Rockstar already confirmed that GTA 6 won't have its own version of the park. That makes sense, too, considering Walt Disney World is located in Orlando and GTA 6 takes place in its own version of Miami, which is more than 200 miles away.

Calls for Grand Theft are not uncommon at Disney World. In October 2026 alone, the County Sheriff's Office received at least seven Grand Theft calls.

One of the most infamous heists at Walt Disney World took place at Epcot. In 2018, thieves nabbed the multi-hundred-pound Buzzy animatronic from the Cranium Command attraction, which was housed at Epcot's shuttered Wonders of Life pavilion.

It has never been recovered. A documentary, Stolen Kingdom, was released in 2025, chronicling the heist and the wider black market for Disney props.

More recently, the Paddlefish restaurant at the Disney World entertainment district, Disney Springs, was robbed by someone who swam up to the waterside restaurant in frogman gear, forced two workers into a corner, obscured the security camera with foam, and made off with cash. This case has not been solved.

In other Disney news, the entertainment giant is teasing "major" announcements for The Game Awards next month. As for GTA 6, the game finally releases on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.

The "We got X before GTA 6" memes have been among the most popular and hilarious over the years as fans waited and waited for the game to release. Even Take-Two's own CEO, Strauss Zelnick, is aware of the memes.

#3577. Avril Lavigne Welcomes Her First Child At Age 42

Avril Lavigne is now a mom. The 42-year-old Canadian might count songs like "Here's to Never Growing Up" among her hits, but in news posted to Instagram Friday, Avril Lavigne revealed a very grown-up milestone.

Beneath a carousel of three black-and-white photos, Lavigne wrote “Our Mini Fucking Princess has arrived,” followed by emojis depicting a baby bottle, a crown, and a pink heart and bow. One photo shows Lavigne cradling an infant dressed in an animal-print onesie and matching headband, while another shows three pairs of Vans on a skateboard. No other details, including information on the baby's name or if Lavigne has a co-parent, were provided.

Avril Lavigne at the Viper Room in the early 2000s.

A spokesperson for the singer told People that “Avril has been enjoying time with her family while working on her new album and wants to thank the fans for all of their love!”

Lavigne has been married twice: once to Canadian guitarist Deryck Whibley and then to Chad Kroeger, the Canadian frontman of the band Nickelback. That latter partnership ended in 2018, but in 2022 she almost tied the knot a third time, with rapper Mod Sun. That relationship ended in 2023.

Mod Sun and Avril Lavigne attend the 2022 MTV Video Music Awards on August 28, 2022

One constant in Lavigne's life has been strong bond she shares with her parents. When, in May 2025, she brought her mother on stage at Madison Square Garden, she wrote on social media: “Ever since I was a little girl, both my mom and dad saw something in me and encouraged me to practice very hard and pursue my dream of becoming a singer/ musician. They made a lot of sacrifices for me and I could not be where I am today without them.”

Continuing, she wrote, “I am grateful to both my parents. Thank you for everything, I love you both!”

Lavigne was still a teenager when her parents allowed her to leave high school to pursue her dream, and her debut at age 17 was a smash hit. Her success continued with singles including 2002's chart-topper “Complicated" and 2021 song “Bite Me.”

Though Friday's announcement was a surprise to most, Lavigne has never been quiet about her desire to become a mom when the time is right. Speaking with E! News in 2013, she laid out her plan: "I want one or two [kids], but not right now," the then-29-year old said. "Like, in the future. Eventually."

#3575. Xbox Game Pass Gets Even More Games In November

The second half of November is usually quiet for several reasons when it comes to new game releases–and one other big reason–but Xbox Game Pass subscribers can look forward to several new titles to close off the month.

Microsoft has announced a handful of new additions to the Game Pass library, including a kid-friendly game to kick things off and a sneak peek at some sporty fun for the first week of December. These announcements typically come in two waves, with a sneak peek split between them, so this list isn't complete yet.

As soon as the rest of the lineup is announced, we’ll update this post with a closer look at what you can download and play soon.

The first game on the way is Paw Patrol: Dino World. Ideal for younger members of the family who definitely shouldn't be playing GTA 6 right now, this family-friendly game revolves around the PAW Patrol working together to round up lost and scared dinosaurs. Starting in December, you can get Freestyle Football 2, which is an online multiplayer soccer game built around 5v5 matches. We already have that game in the form of Rematch from Sifu developer Sloclap, but if you want a different spin on that soccer idea, take a quick look.

Xbox Game Pass November Wave 2 Games

November 17

  • Paw Patrol: Dino World (Xbox Series X|S, PC)

December 3

  • Freestyle Football 2 (Xbox Series X|S, PC)

November has been pretty good for new entries in the Game Pass library, with the start of the month bringing the dungeon-crawling roguelike deck-building game Dungeon Crawlers to more Game Pass tiers, while subscribers also got Void/Breaker, Warhammer Survivors, and John Carpenter’s Toxic Commando. Game Pass Essential saw a big influx of new games, with several Banjo-Kazooie titles joining People Can Fly’s Gears of War prequel and the beloved Viva Piñata games.

Spoilers ahead about the most recent episode of The Great British Baking Show.

I love reality TV, although most of the shows I watch are cutthroat like Survivor, The Traitors, or the Real Housewives. I decided to watch The Great British Baking Show for the first time this year with my Netflix subscription, and have loved how charming and wholesome the series is in comparison. As such, I was surprised when the latest episode legit made me cry, largely thanks to how much Moyin was crying over Connie's elimination. Luckily there is a silver lining with this heartbreak.

Bake Off has been a joy to watch, from Nigella Lawson's passion for eating to the kindness the contestants extend to each other. Last week's Pastry Week had my mouth watering, but for Caramel Week it was my eyes that was producing the moisture. I was bummed to see Connie eliminated, but it was the way Moyin was weeping that had me feeling misty. I mean, just look at these two.

While the cast of Bake Off all formed sweet bonds (pun intended), Moyim and Connie were on another level. Throughout the season they were shown getting close, forming a mother/son relationship in the process. They'd also help each other's bakes when needed, despite competing against each other.

Moyim's emotional reaction to Connie's elimination was moving, as he was devastated despite winning Star Baker. I was left in a puddle by the time the latest episode ended, but luckily the franchise cheered me up thanks to some delightful content of their reunion. Case in point: the following video from Bake Off's official Instagram account. Check it out for yourself below.

A post shared by The Great British Bake Off (@britishbakeoff)

I mean, how adorable are these two? Clearly their bond extends outside of the Bake Off tent, and they've remained close in the time between filming and the current season airing. It would have been heartwarming enough to merely see Connie and Moyin reuniting, but the fact that they showed off their dance moves in the above video is even more delightful. So while the latest episode of The Great British Baking Show made me cry, I'm back to enjoying the show's immense charm.

From the premiere of Bake Off's season, it seemed like the cooling process was going to be a challenge for the bakers in the midst of a heat wave across the pond. That proved challenging for Connie during Caramel Week, and after fumbling both the Signature and Showstopper, Connie was ultimately eliminated. Cue the tears.

New episodes of The Great British Baking Show air Fridays on Netflix as part of the 2026 TV schedule. We'll just have to see if the remainder of the season makes me cry again, or if it'll stay charming and wholesome.

#3573. Los Javis Are “Living a Dream” As La Bola Negra with Penélope Cruz, Guitarricadelafuente, and Miguel Bernardeau Collects Honors

While La Bola Negra continues to amass various accolades and early awards, like the Best Director award at this year's Cannes Film Festival and the Audience Award at the Toronto International Film Festival, directors Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvo are extra grateful and overwhelmed by the film's reception and success in their home country of Spain.

Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvo at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026

“You can't plan the miracle,” Calvo said during a panel conversation moderated by Ricky Martin at the inaugural Vanity Fair Screening Room at LACMA on Friday. “We’ve done many projects and each one of them has, they've all been good, but you never know when it's going to happen. And with La Bola Negra, we thought it was a very specific story and we thought that our audience was going to like it, but we never knew it was going to hit everyone. I think it's about to become the second highest grossing movie in the history of Spain. For me, the most beautiful part of it is the videos of the people hugging after the screenings, giving tissues to each other, comforting each other.”

La Bola Negra follows several gay men whose lives are bound together by their identities, love and loss, and the looming presence of the Spanish Civil War. The acclaimed Spanish language drama spans nearly a century and stars Miguel Bernardeau, Álvaro Lafuente Calvo (the singer known as Guitarricadelafuente) in his first major acting role, Carlos Gonzalez, Milo Quifes and Penélope Cruz.

Guitarricadelafuente at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026

Following an exclusive screening of the film on Friday, Martin moderated a panel conversation featuring directors Ambrossi and Calvo, and stars Cruz, Guitarricadelafuente and Bernardeau. Calvo said they are all riding high on the positive audience reactions and reception. “Creating this sense of community and hearing people saying, ‘This movie changed me. It really made me understand things about me.’ The power that art has, we forget it, but then this happens and … the rest is a dream. The rest we're living is a dream.”

The directors also consider having Cruz play a small but pivotal role in the film to be part of their living a dream. When Martin asked Cruz how her longstanding allyship to the LGBTQ+ community shaped her intention or performance, she said, “I don't even ask myself that question because it's such a part of me, of the way that I was raised. My very young parents, my parents had me when they were 21. It was a house where the values were about respect and it was just like breathing. They didn't even have to sit us down and give us a lecture about it, it was the way my family was living by example. And on top of that, then I had my other master Pedro Almodóvar who I've worked with for seven movies. And I always remember growing up thinking, why is he not the president of our country? Because he was huge in a time where his presence was really necessary, not only through his films, but also by the things that he was saying. So I feel like all of that has shaped me.”

Miguel Bernardeau, Guitarricadelafuente, Penélope Cruz, Javier Calvo, Javier Ambrossi and Ricky Martin at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026

She continued: “So when I have in my hands the possibility of playing somebody like Nené Romero, that is a reminder that unfortunately not everyone in the world feels the way we feel about everyone having a right for respect, everyone having a right to be themselves.”

Ricky Martin at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026

For Martin, a Bola Negra superfan who admitted he was nervous to be asking questions instead of answering them, the actor and musician said he found out about his hosting opportunity only the day before and despite the nerves couldn't pass up the opportunity to help celebrate the film.

“I usually answer the questions, I never ask the questions, but I needed to be here,” he told the audience. “I saw this film and for a while I was in the movie. I was really touched. The acting, the way it was written, people are crying because that's just the way it is, [really moving].”

Miguel Bernardeau at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026

The inaugural edition of Vanity Fair’s Screening Room pairs this year’s most compelling films with a slate of programming that includes post-screening panels and conversations with actors and filmmakers. The invitation-only events are welcoming an audience from the worlds of film, fashion, culture, politics, media, and tech, much like the magazine itself.

Following the program in Los Angeles, Vanity Fair’s Screening Room will arrive in New York, where screenings and events will take place at Cherry Lane Theatre from December 4–6.

#3572. Shooting Suspect In Custody After Opening Fire Near Xbox Dev’s Studio

A drive-by shooting in Southern California ended with no injuries and an arrest after the gunman reportedly opened fire near a business and office campus that houses Xbox subsidiary InXile Entertainment.

According to Aftermath and local affiliate KTLA5, the shooting occurred on November 11 at an office building on the former Marine Corps Air Station in Tustin, California. The police department posted on Facebook that, after uncovering "multiple shell casings in the area," local detectives worked "around the clock" to locate the suspect.

Sergeant Christopher Peterson told Aftermath on November 13 that although the investigation is still ongoing, an unnamed suspect had been apprehended "less than 48 hours" after the shooting.

"Officers got there [on November 11]," Sergeant Peterson said. "They responded to a report of a drive-by shooting there. Located multiple shell casings. Nobody was hurt. Processed the crime scene, and then sometime [Friday] morning, a little before 11 [AM], they took a suspect into custody. And the investigation is still kind of ongoing as to where and why."

An InXile Entertainment spokesperson corroborated the incident with Aftermath, expressing relief about the situation.

"We're relieved that no one was hurt at our inXile office,” the spokesperson said. "Our focus is on supporting our team, and we are working closely with law enforcement as they investigate."

Founded in 2002, InXile Entertainment has been under the Xbox Game Studios umbrella since 2018. Since its founding, the studio has developed several games, from the 2004 ARPG The Bard's Tale to the 2011 action-adventure Hunted: The Demon's Forge to the 2014 post-apocalyptic RPG Wasteland 2. Currently, the team is working on Clockwork Revolution, a steampunk ARPG not too dissimilar from immersive sims like BioShock and Dishonored. It has no release date right now, but InXile Entertainment is targeting a 2027 window for PC and Xbox Series X|S.
