#3546. Five Creative Ways to Spend Your FSA Funds Before the End of the Year

If you have a flexible spending account (FSA), you know the drill: Use the funds before the end of the year, or lose them. Unfortunately, chances are slim you can pack the rest of the year with doctor's appointments. Does that mean your hard-earned funds go to waste? Definitely not. You can spend your remaining FSA funds on other qualifying healthcare costs. And what counts as "qualifying" might surprise you—for instance, you can use your FSA or HSA funds to get yourself a sweet new fitness tracker or smartwatch.

As the end of the year approaches, here are all the ways you can spend any leftover money in your FSA balance.

Many over-the-counter medications and health items are FSA-eligible, including pain relievers, cold medicine, bandages, dental care products, menstrual products, and more. Scan your medicine cabinet and make a list of anything you need to stock up on.

FSA/HSA eligibility for smartwatches and other fitness wearables is real, but the main “catch" (as I’ve previously explained) is proving the device is in fact necessary, which requires you to obtain a Letter of Medical Necessity (LMN).

Screenless recovery trackers like Whoop, Amazfit Helio Strap, and the Oura Ring can usually be justified as HSA/FSA eligible around sleep quality, HRV-based stress monitoring, or recovery tracking tied to a chronic condition. Similarly, smartwatches can qualify the same way a basic tracker does, as long as you can link a relevant documented health concern. For instance, Coros offers FSA/HSA eligibility for all its watches and heart rate monitors through its partnership with Truemed. Amazfit similarly lets you filter by HSA/FSA eligibility for its smartwatches.

If you want to get creative with it, the official FSA store lets you filter by "surprisingly eligible." Similar to the section above, for some of these items, you'll want to brush up on how exactly to get an LMN to justify certain tech as FSA-eligible for you personally. In the meantime, go crazy and snag yourself Epsom salt for $8.99, Supergoop! sunscreen for $38.00, or perhaps a snazzy massage gun for $349.99.

Knee braces, wrist splints, compression socks, and other orthopedic items can help relieve chronic pain issues. Rather than wait for these issues to rear their heads down the line, use FSA money to offset the costs of these fixes now. If you use eyeglasses or contacts, consider using your FSA dollars to update or refresh your prescriptions. Don't forget to stock up on eye drops and lens solution, too.

If you have medical procedures scheduled for early next year, many healthcare providers will allow you to pre-pay the estimated costs this calendar year using FSA funds. This includes dental work, physical therapy, chiropractic visits, Lasik eye surgery, and more.

However you choose to spend your FSA funds, don’t let that money go to waste. After all, it came out of your paycheck. Check in with your employer’s rules for any balance remaining on Dec. 31 this year, so you aren’t left forfeiting your hard-earned funds. You can find a complete list at the FSA store here.

#3545. Penélope Cruz Says She and Husband Javier Bardem are “Very Careful” About Choosing When to Work Together

Penélope Cruz and Javier Bardem are very selective about when they work on a project together, but the opportunity to costar in director Florian Zeller's timely psychological thriller Bunker was too enticing to pass up.

"When [Zeller] came to us with this powerful, very necessary story to tell, we looked at each other and there was no way to say no to this," Cruz said during a post-screening discussion at Vanity Fair’s Screening Room on Sunday. "I'm very, very happy that we did it."

Bunker revolves around a married couple, Miguel (Bardem) and Sofia (Cruz), whose 17-year marriage is tested when Miguel, a famous architect, is presented with a life changing work opportunity.

“I really wanted to work with them because I truly believe they are [two] of the greatest actors working today,” Zeller said during the panel discussion moderated by VF's West Coast Editor John Ross. “I was also very excited and interested to have them together onscreen because they are also a real couple. I thought it would be an interesting and unique opportunity to approach something that has to do with authenticity, with the truth. Not to say that this is their story, because of course this is not their story.”

Florian Zeller at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 15, 2026

Cruz said she felt a kinship with her character's concerns. “We have so many things in common in terms of this sadness and frustration and anger that you feel in terms of where is the world going if we don't wake up soon,” she said. “I hope it's not too late, but especially the experiment that is being done on younger people, children, teenagers, it just makes me very furious.

“It's something that affects me so much as an actress, as a mother, as a citizen of the world, that I felt completely a need to play Sophia,” she continued. “And of course it was not the only reason, but it was a big privilege to be able to say those lines. And [Zeller] is such a master of writing and I am a fan of all his work. And same for Javier, who is not here with us today, he's doing theater, but we are very careful in terms of choosing when to work together.”

Pénelope Cruz, Florian Zeller and John Ross at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 15, 2026

Cruz praised Zeller’s ability to provide a supportive, safe working environment and his strong point of view. “We felt really, really safe with him, he's so talented. He doesn't need any kind of manipulation and he never treats the audience as not intelligent because the audience can feel everything,” she explained. “And that has become really the most important thing for me. Don't over-explain, don't underestimate the audience ever because the thermometer is really working. And also with young people more and more and more. That is my hope to continue to go to see films on a big screen. They're coming back thank God. So let's create more possibilities so they can keep doing that.”

Cruz also said that she and Bardem have similar approaches to their work and the preparation it requires. “It's true that we share the same passion and we have done this since we were teenagers,” she said. “We love exploring and studying and feeling that healthy fear of the unknown because every time you begin a project, in a way, it's really starting from zero. So it's a really good thing to share.”

Zeller called his collaboration with the couple “a fascinating journey. It takes a lot of courage or fearlessness to do that, I think, for actors.” He also revealed that he initially referenced Stanley Kubrick's seminal thriller Eyes Wide Shut as a point of reference for Bunker, but realized it might not be setting the proper tone, given the circumstances.

“I remember that the first time I spoke with [Cruz] and Javier about this project, I mentioned a film that was somewhere in my mind, Eyes Wide Shut. Not to say that there is any kind of connection between the two films, but as you remember, Eyes Wide Shut at the time, Tom Cruise and Nicole Kidman, they were together," he said. "And I remember as a viewer that it was so interesting to be in a position where you do not know exactly what you're invited to watch… but Javier [later] told me, ‘You should not mention this film too often because remember at the end of the shooting they broke up.’ And then I realized that the director, Kubrick, died soon after. So I was like, ‘Okay, I'm going to stop mentioning this film.’ But the real difference I would say is that we knew that the destination of that film was the last image of the painting that you saw, which means that it was about how to reconnect with the other.”

Pénelope Cruz, Florian Zeller and John Ross at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 15, 2026

The inaugural edition of Vanity Fair’s Screening Room pairs this year’s most compelling films with a slate of programming that includes post-screening panels and conversations with actors and filmmakers. The invitation-only events are welcoming an audience from the worlds of film, fashion, culture, politics, media, and tech, much like the magazine itself.

Following the program in Los Angeles, Vanity Fair’s Screening Room will arrive in New York, where screenings and events will take place at Cherry Lane Theatre from December 4–6.

The Lavazza Tabli is the "It" girl of 2026

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

I'm Erin, and welcome to The Coffee Lab Episode 25, the series where we forget coffee snobbery. The Coffee Lab is all about making coffee fun. Join me as I help you kickstart your coffee journey!

Here at The Coffee Lab, I'm always eager to get my hands on the newest and most exciting coffee tech. So when I saw a commercial for the Lavazza Tabli on YouTube, I was instantly smitten. Yes. A commercial worked on me — I was influenced!

A few days later, I had the Lavazza Tabli in my hands, and everything was right in the world. At first, I needed to know how. How did the Lavazza Tabli work? If you're not sure what it does, let me give you a quick introduction: it's a pod machine... that doesn't use pods.

That's right. The Tabli uses 100% coffee "Tabs," shaped like hockey pucks, rather than plastic- or aluminum-encased ground coffee. This coffee is compacted so tightly that it keeps its shape. And don't wrinkle your nose — this coffee tastes genuinely incredible. I'm a hard-to-please coffee snob, and I've been singing the Tabli's praises since I tested it a few weeks ago. Here's why the Lavazza Tabli is one of my favorite coffee makers of 2026 — perhaps ever.

Of course, no one's claiming the Lavazza Tabli can make espresso better than a machine like the Lelit MaraX3, single-origin artisan beans, and a talented barista. That would be outrageous and untrue.

However, I am claiming that the Lavazza Tabli tastes a thousand times better than the best Keurig — I just tested the Keurig K-Mini Mate, and while it's tiny and easy, I would rather drink instant — and ten times better than the best Nespresso. Obviously, I don't have quantitative data to back that up, but can I interest you in a decibel counter for the volume of "Mmm" noises I made while drinking said coffees? Because the Tabli surely would win.

Unlike Nespresso and Keurig, Lavazza has just five "Tab" flavors: espresso intenso, qualita rossa, qualita oro, ristretto, and decaf. My favorite was oro. While Nespresso tastes so much better than Keurig, Nespresso shots are still a touch weak and stale, without the vivaciousness on the palate I look for in espresso.

This inexpensive machine uses compressed pucks of grounds to make some truly tasty coffee — without the wasteful pods.

The Tabli? Oh-so vivacious. So vivacious, in fact, that I would equate it to a party on my tongue. The shot is strong and full-bodied, like any Italian coffee tends to be, but with a delicate sweetness rounding out the mouthful. While the flavor depends on your "Tab", both the oro and the rossa were punchy yet delightfully drinkable.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

I said this in my review, and I'll say it again, but I do wonder if, in time, Lavazza will introduce some kind of Tab-making machine: a press or compacter of some kind, so you can make your own "Tabs". That would be awesome. Catch me making coffee snobs choke on their espressos when I grind single-origin Yirgacheffe into Lavazza Tabs. Ha!

Like Nespresso and Keurig machines, the Lavazza Tabli requires zero cleanup. Well, unless you count removing a pod drawer and emptying it into your compost/trash as cleanup. I'm not sure I would.

Using the Tabli is as easy as this: pop a pod in, press go, drink coffee, empty drawer. Sure, you should probably clean the pod insert after every use, and you should definitely clean out the pod drawer every day (coffee gets moldy quickly), but in terms of scooping-out-wet-grounds-from-a-portafilter-basket-and-emptying-a-milky-drip-tray cleaning, it's minimal.

Although I adore everything about the Lavazza Tabli, there are still a few things I would recommend being aware of before biting the bullet.

One being the most obvious: the Tabli is only compatible with Lavazza-brand Tabs (for now). These are a dollar a pop, in line with Nespresso's original pods (around $0.90-$1) and cheaper than the Vertuo pods (up to $1.40 in some flavors). Keurig pods are around $0.50-$0.70 — but remember you can't recycle them for free, so you're out of pocket for caring about the planet. Great! Thanks, Keurig. Nothing says "There is no planet B" like forcing consumers to pay to recycle the plastic pods you make en masse.

Nespresso original and Keurig pods aren't patented, unlike Vertuo, so third parties can manufacture pods in a whole array of flavors.

The Lavazza Tabli machine itself is patented, which I presume extends to the Tabs themselves (boo! — but I get it). This means, if you buy the Tabli, you're locked into buying Lavazza's Tabs — just like a Nespresso Vertuo.

Right now, Lavazza only offers those five core flavors, so no specialty Tabs like fall favorite pumpkin spice or Christmas classics like eggnog or Irish cream. Of course, you can buy syrups to add to your drinks, but Nespresso makes flavored pods. This might be something worth knowing if you're a flavored coffee fanatic.

Would you try the Lavazza Tabli? Or do you love your Nespresso/Keurig machine too much to part with it?

I would personally buy the Lavazza Tabli. Oh yeah — I saved the best 'til last. It's just $129. No, not a typo. Yes, $129. This is almost incomprehensibly cheap... in the best way. The Nespresso CitiZ is $265, the Nespresso Pixie is $229, and the Keurig K-Supreme is $169.

#3543. The Biggest Snubs and Surprises From the 2027 Grammy Nominations

The 2027 Grammy nominations are here, and not everyone in the music industry is celebrating.

Recording Academy CEO Harvey Mason Jr. and board of trustees chairperson Dr. Chelsey Green woke up bright and early on Monday, November 16, to reveal the nominees for music’s biggest night.

With help from a star-studded crop of past honorees including Carly Pearce, David Guetta, Kehlani and Olivia Dean, fans learned Raye received the most nominations with 11.

Other musicians, however, were disappointed to learn they didn’t receive any love from the Recording Academy.

“Life goes on,” Noah Kahan wrote via X on Monday, seemingly referencing his one nomination for The Great Divide.

Keep reading to see the biggest snubs and surprises, and make sure to watch the 2027 Grammy Awards on ABC February 7, 2027, from Los Angeles’ Crypto.com Arena.

Styles kicked off a successful year in March when he released Kiss All the Time. Disco, Occasionally. The album featured massive hits, including “Aperture” and “American Girls.”

Ultimately, it wasn’t enough for the former One Direction member to receive a nomination. At least he still has his Album of the Year trophy for Harry’s House.

After Kahan’s latest album, The Great Divide, reached No. 1 on the Billboard 200, many fans were expecting the artist to receive multiple nominations.

Ultimately, Kahan only received a nod in the Best Contemporary Folk Album category. “Life goes on,” he wrote via X hours after the nominations were revealed.

It was a year to remember for the country singer, who released her debut album, earned a massive hit with “Boston” and was favored to earn a Best New Artist nomination.

While she may not be receiving a Grammy trophy in early 2027, she is joining Morgan Wallen as a supporting act on his massive Last Time I Checked Tour stadium run.

Despite a massive sold-out arena tour, Summit did not receive any love from the Recording Academy on nomination day.

“Never submitting to the grammys again unless s*** changes, it’s all a f***ing joke,” the DJ wrote via X on Monday. “I’m not just talking about myself either. There’s zero respect for real electronic dance music & dj’s. the whole dance category is just music industry fueled pop stars.”

In a separate post, Summit wrote, “Not saying the artists nominated aren’t good, they’re just not dance music, they’re pop. No dj is playing that music in the clubs.”

The former Best New Artist nominee failed to snag any nominations for her latest album, Daughter From Hell, which included her single “Hit the Wall.”

Abrams still has a reason to celebrate: The body of work was her first No. 1 album on the Billboard 200.

After a nearly two-year hiatus, West scored a nomination for Best Rap Album thanks to Bully. Fans can now prepare themselves for another possible must-see red carpet look with the artist and his wife, Bianca Censori.

Madonna earned her first Grammy nominations in nearly 16 years. Her categories include Best Pop Duo/Group Performance for “Bring Your Love” with Sabrina Carpenter and Best Dance/Electronic Album for Confessions II.

It’s also the most nominations the Queen of Pop has received for a single album since 1999. However, many fans were disappointed to see Confessions II was not up for Album of the Year.

After years of hard work, Tinashe woke up to the news that she scored her first Grammy nominations. Her categories include Best Dance/Electronic Recording for “Melatonin” and Best Dance Pop Recording for “Too Easy.”

“From underrated to GRAMMY NOMINATED bitchhhhhhh omgggggggggggggggg 😭😭😭😭😭😭,” she wrote via her Instagram.

The country icon is still being celebrated after her death in August at the age of 80. Parton received three posthumous nominations, including Best Country Duo/Group Performance for “Here” with Zac Brown Band and “Light of a Clear Blue Morning” with Lainey Wilson, Miley Cyrus, Queen Latifah and Reba McEntire.

#3542. These 10 New Features Are Coming to iOS 27.3

Apple dropped the first developer beta for iOS 27.3 on Tuesday. While this update isn't as large as iOS 27 proper, it's surprisingly feature-filled for a 0.3 update. This is only a beta, so anything could (and likely will) change before Apple officially launches the update. But, as it stands, iOS 27.3 tests 10 new features—including one feature the company trialed in the previous beta.

Technically, anyone with a compatible iPhone can try out iOS 27.3 right now—assuming you enroll your Apple Account in the developer program. But a word of warning: Betas can be temperamental, and could be risky. As such, I'd recommend avoiding the beta until Apple releases the public beta, which comes after a bit more testing to iron out larger issues. Either way, make sure to make a full backup of your iPhone to a Mac or PC first, as issues with the beta could result in permanent data loss.

With watchOS 27, Apple released "Audio Intelligence," a new set of features for Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4. Audio Intelligence uses the watches' new S11 chip, along with on-device AI and cloud-based AI, to run new features, like Sound Recognition and Shazam (music recognition).

With iOS 27.3, however, the company is now officially testing the other two Audio Intelligence features it originally announced with watchOS 27. First, there's Live Rewind: By double-clicking the watch crown, you can pull up a transcript of the last 15 seconds of a conversation. Siri Recap, on the other hand, displays summaries of conversations you had that day, in case you need a refresher on any chats you might have otherwise forgotten about,

The company generated some controversy when it first announced these two Audio Intelligence features, since, on the surface, it sounds like these new Apple Watches are essentially spying on people all day long. According to Apple, however, that isn't really the case. The company says Audio Intelligence is private, and never records or stores any audio. No speakers are ever identified, and text results (both transcripts and summaries) are deleted automatically after a set period of time unless the user saves them to the Siri app. You can read more about how Audio Intelligence works here.

Despite their claims, I'm sure there will still be strong feelings surrounding these Audio Intelligence features. We'll have to see whether Apple can prove Live Rewind and Siri Recap aren't all that creepy throughout the iOS 27.3 beta process.

iOS 27.3 also introduces app actions for Siri AI. Apple is testing new abilities for Siri AI, including organizing files, planning events, or adding photos to albums. You could ask Siri to organize your Downloads folder, or delete files that haven't been opened in more than a year. You could ask Siri to find a coffee shop you went to last week, or to save an article to your Reading List in Safari. You could ask Siri to check your calendar and set up a time for an event based on when you're free. You can even ask the assistant to schedule, edit, or unsend messages.

For example, you could ask Siri AI to help you plan a trip with your friends. You could ask the AI to put together a themed playlist in Apple Music, schedule a message to a group about an upcoming trip, organize the websites you've been visiting in Safari into a tab group, and, after the trip, ask Siri to move your best photos to your favorites album. These new actions work in the following apps: Calendar, Files, Finder, Journal, Mail, Maps, Messages, Music, Notes, Photos, Preview, Reminders, Safari, Shortcuts, and Weather. Developers can also add Siri AI app actions support to their own apps.

Apple started testing its new Health app with the iOS 27.2 beta, but pulled the redesign before the official release. Now, with iOS 27.3, the new app is back. The new Health app has a health dashboard for the first time, as well as new features like Health Age and movement assessments. It seems to be pulling from some popular competitor services, hopefully, for the better. For more on the new Health app, check out Lifehacker health editor Beth Skwarecki's explainer.

Continuing on the Health track, iOS 27.3 also introduces "Gym Strength." This is a new Fitness+ feature that offers a personalized four-week strength-training plan. You can customize these plans to meet your goals, experience level, and schedule, and they adapt as you progress. You'll get recommendations based on your experience with exercises, reps, and sets, including video demos for exercises. You can access Gym Strength on both iPhone and iPad, and Apple Watches are optional—though you can log your progress with the wearable if you have it.

Vertical tabs have been a favorite among browser aficionados, as they give you more screen real estate in your browser while keeping your tabs off the side. Apple hasn't made the jump—until now. This feature works with iPads running iPadOS 27.3 as well as Macs running macOS 27.3.

Another new Safari feature in testing is "Adaptive Dark Mode." This feature forces websites into a dark theme, if they don't have a native theme of their own. There are third-party apps that can do this, but this is the first time Apple has offered this feature built into Safari.

Apple is also testing new StandBy experiences with iOS 27.3, which were previously only available on the iPhone Duo. When you turn your iPhone sideways while plugged in, you'll find new Analog and Digital Clock faces with new customization options. There's also a new Photos face, with the option to pull images from Shared Albums.

"Reachability" pulls your iPhone's display down towards the bottom of the screen, so you can access items towards the top of the display with one hand. It's a useful feature for those of us with big iPhones, and now, there's no iPhone bigger than the Duo. With iOS 27.3, Apple is testing Reachability for its first foldable phone. It's a bit like the inverse of how Reachability currently works: You can swipe on the left or right side of your Duo's display to shift the other side of the screen towards your current position. If you're holding your Duo in your left hand, a swipe of the left side will pull the right side over to the left, and vice versa.

Apple is also rolling out new languages for Siri AI in iOS 27.3. Now, Apple's smart assistant supports Traditional Chinese, Vietnamese, Turkish, and Norwegian.

If you have an Apple Intelligence-compatible iPad running iPadOS 27.3, you now have access to Siri Mode in Camera. As with iOS, you can open the Camera app on iPadOS to access Siri Mode, and ask Siri about your surroundings.

Bari Weiss’ tenure as the editor-in-chief of CBS News has sparked a myriad of responses from media pundits and the general public, who’ve taken issue with the organization’s content. While Weiss has received praise in some circles, she’s also been critiqued for some of her decisions, including those made in regard to 60 Minutes. Even now, some continue to chastise her editorial and staffing choices for the news magazine show. All the while, it seems Weiss is embroiled in some reported drama involving another news program.

Just recently, Weiss was at the center of a report involving Face the Nation, one of CBS News’ key political programs. According to this update, Weiss apparently planned to part ways with the aforementioned show’s moderator, Margaret Brennan. The media newsletter Status (via The New York Post) didn’t specify why Weiss opted to retain Brennan. At this point, Brennan has headlined FTN since 2018 and, in addition to that she serves as the network’s chief of foreign affairs and fills in as an anchor on CBS Evening News.

Although Brennan is still with the show, it just lost two key members of its team. Senior executive producer Mary Hager recently announced that she would depart CBS News after 25 years with the network. Another key detail about this move is that since 2022, Hager has served as the executive director of politics for the Eye Network and has overseen its Washington Bureau. FTN executive producer Anne Hsu is leaving the show but, unlike Hager, she’ll remain with CBS and will head up its Hong Kong bureau.

These major exits mark the end of another era for Face the Nation, which debuted back in 1954 and, as of right now, it’s unclear just how Weiss will proceed in regard to filling those posts. With this, the Free Press founder finds herself in another staffing situation just months after her overhaul of 60 Minutes. And that series of personnel changes is still being discussed as part of the backlash that 60 has received as of late.

Ex-60 Minutes EP On His Biggest Concerns Amid Bari Weiss’ Leadership: ‘That Would Have Freaked Me Out’

Earlier this year, Anderson Cooper exited his correspondent post at 60 Minutes after nearly two decades, citing a desire to have more time to spend with his loved ones. It was subsequently reported, however, that Cooper’s departure was partially due to disagreements with Weiss. Shortly after Cooper’s move, Weiss and series EP Nick Bilton fired correspondents Cecilia Vega and Sharyn Alfonsi along with former EP Tanya Simon and several others. Correspondent Scott Pelley was also fired days later after reportedly accusing Weiss of “murdering” the show.

In the aftermath, Weiss brought in a roster of new talent to join series veterans Lesley Stahl, Bill Whitaker and Jon Wertheim. Pundits like Ross Douthat, Ariel Levy and Sir Trevor Phillips were brought in to fill out the staff. All the while, Weiss continues to receive backlash for those staffing changes, and she’s also been on the receiving end of news bias allegations (which she’s denied). Additionally, 60’s low ratings amid Season 59 have also been a point of contention among critics.

Bari Weiss addressed the 60 Minutes concerns just weeks ago and claimed the show had been doing “tremendously well.” Several staffers including Tony Dokoupil and Norah O’Donnell have also defended Weiss against backlash. In terms of Face the Nation, it’ll be interesting to see how Weiss plans to tap for those big producer jobs. Time will also tell whether Weiss chooses to revisit her reported plan to cut ties with Margaret Brennan.

Robot vacuums have been around a while, but it can still be tough to find one that is also good at mopping. But unlike many robot vacuum and mop combos that use spinning pads, the all-in-one Eufy E25 robot vacuum and mop has a self-cleaning roller mop: The roller is rinsed with clean water as it mops, then cleaned at the dock, meaning you don't need to spend as much time cleaning it yourself. It's a smart design, and it's a great time to pick one up: Right now, the E25 is 40% off in an early Black Friday deal at Amazon, taking it down to $599.98 (originally $999.99).

Users can map an area, set zones, schedule cleans, and define different features via the Eufy Clean app; the customizable options include cleaning intensity, suction power, water level, and deciding whether you want the E25 to make multiple passes in an area.  It uses LiDAR mapping and AI for obstacle detection and is highly automated, with a dock that empties the robot, washes and dries the roller mop, and refills its water supply. If you live in a home with pets and want a low-maintenance robot vacuum and mop that can handle routine floor cleaning with minimal intervention, the Eufy E25 can cut some serious time from your cleaning routine.

#3539. Man Told Neighbor He 'Killed His Girl' After Allegedly Strangling 91-Year-Old

A Florida man knocked on a neighbor’s door and revealed he killed his longtime friend immediately after he allegedly strangled the woman for approximately 10 minutes and became shocked when she was no longer breathing, police said.

Victor Dorantes-Velazquez was arrested Sunday, November 15, on a first-degree murder charge in connection with the woman’s death, according to arrest paperwork filed in court.

Officers called to a “suspicious incident” at the suspect’s Hallandale Beach apartment on Saturday, November 14, found Dorantes-Velazquez, 77, sitting in a chair in his living room, next to a bed where a 91-year-old woman was in the fetal position, unresponsive, per a probable cause affidavit obtained by Us.

The woman, who Dorantes-Velazquez described as his friend of several years, was declared dead, the affidavit states.

According to Dorantes-Velazquez’s sworn statement, he confronted and strangled the woman on Saturday after accusing her of stealing items he discovered were missing, including his car keys, phone and a brown wallet with more than $1,000 in cash.

The woman, who had been living with Dorantes-Velazquez for a few months, denied the theft and kept laughing at him as he confronted her about his missing items throughout the day, Dorantes-Velazquez told police.

Dorantes-Velazquez “advised at one point, as he continued asking for his property back, the victim began yelling at him” and also “tried to scratch him,” a detective wrote in the affidavit.

He allegedly held her down onto the bed by her shoulders before she tried to grab pill bottles to throw at him, according to Dorantes-Velazquez’s sworn statement.

Dorantes-Velazquez said he “lost his temper” and began to strangle his friend, per the affidavit.

“[She] told [Dorantes-Velazquez] to let her go and she would give him his belongings so [Dorantes-Velazquez] released his grip at which time [she] began laughing at [him],” an officer rewrote in the affidavit, adding that this caused Dorantes-Velazquez to “lose control.”

The woman tried to fight him off as he allegedly strangled her for about 10 minutes until she appeared motionless and didn’t seem to be breathing, according to the affidavit.

Dorantes-Velazquez told police he was “shocked” and took an elevator to the apartment building’s fourth floor, where he knocked on a neighbor’s unit to seek help.

The neighbor said in his statement to police that Dorantes-Velazquez “asked him to call 911 because he had killed his girl,” the affidavit states.

Afterward, the neighbor and another resident followed Dorantes-Velazquez to the elevator.

According to the affidavit, while inside the elevator, Dorantes-Velazquez allegedly confessed, “I grabbed her by her neck and killed her because she took my wallet and money.”

After the elevator doors opened, Dorantes-Velazquez went to another woman and asked her to call 911, the affidavit states.

Dorantes-Velazquez is detained at the North Broward Bureau detention facility in Broward County, records show.

Information on whether he retained legal counsel wasn’t immediately available.

#3538. My Favorite Sony Headphones Are Over $80 Off Right Now

One of the best headphone deals right now is for my favorite headphones: Sony's 1000X series has been around since 2016, with each new model improving on the previous iteration, the latest being the Sony WH-1000XM6, released in 2025. These are the best over-ear headphones I tested in 2025 (or ever, really). Right now, you can get the WH-1000XM6 headphones for $378 (originally $459.99), their lowest price ever, according to price-tracking tools.

The XM6 headphones improve on what were already excellent headphones. Sony upped the count of microphones from eight to 12 when compared to the XM5, which improves more than just how well you sound to someone on a phone call. The microphones are used in almost all of its features, like ANC, Adaptive Sound Control, and the headphones' Ambient Sound mode. They hear your surroundings to adapt their features accordingly. If you switch from a noisy room to a quiet one, the XM6 can switch from ANC to aware mode (if you have Adaptive Sound Control on).

These headphones have a lot more features that you can nerd out on in their companion app. The audio quality is second to none, with the fully customizable EQ giving you plenty of options to get the sound how you like it. I really like being able to see what codec you're listening to in the app's main menu. That way, there's no guessing if you're getting the best audio quality or not. They will give you 30 hours of battery life with ANC on and 40 hours of juice with ANC off. There's an AUX (3.5mm) jack for wired listening, which is a nice touch for audiophiles who still rock iPod Classics (or is that just me?).

The XM6s were not just the best headphones of 2025, but are still the best ones of 2026 and likely to be the best ones for years to come. For $378, you'll be securing the best for a record-low price.

A price drop always stands out more when the product in question already has a reputation for delivering above its size, and that’s the case with the Bose SoundLink Plus. It hasn’t been on the market for long, but it’s already earned strong reviews—CNET labeled it “the Goldilocks of Bose Bluetooth speakers.” And right now, ahead of Black Friday, it’s down to $179 from $269, which price trackers show is the lowest it’s ever been.

Bose positions it right in the middle of the SoundLink lineup, and you feel that balance in how it’s built. It’s compact enough to clip onto a backpack using its built-in nylon strap, and tough enough to handle getting knocked around, and sealed against dust and full water submersion with an IP67 rating. Battery life can last up to 20 hours, depending on the volume, which is sufficient for full-day outings. On the connectivity side, there’s Bluetooth 5.4 with AAC and AptX Adaptive support, as well as the ability to keep two devices paired for smoother switching. What you don’t get is a microphone, an aux port, or any voice assistant support, which is worth considering if you prefer wired options or use speakers for calls.

As for its sound profile, it leans into mid- and high-bass, which gives electronic and pop tracks a lively pulse, though at higher volumes, you may notice some compression (which is common in speakers this size). It also doesn’t reach into true low-bass territory, so anyone who wants thumping sub-bass may not get it here, but the punch it does deliver feels clean for its size, notes this PCMag review. And while you won't get the width and separation of a stereo mix since the SoundLink Plus plays audio in mono, its directivity is good—meaning its sound remains clear from different listening positions, so you don't have to sit directly in front of it to get a good experience.

Danny Kilby showed on Survivor that he had guts after threatening to go to rocks to keep ally Lewis Kelly safe. That was bold, but I never would've imagined he'd be so bold as to execute that exact strategy in a bid to win back all his belongings after Season 51. Unfortunately, his attempt to recreate Storage Wars ended in disaster, but it makes for a hilarious story.

Kilby posted on TikTok about how he moved out of his apartment before Survivor and put all his furniture possessions in a storage locker. Unfortunately, just before leaving, he got a new debit card and realized he forgot to change his billing information with the facility. He said:

So I call them, I spam them, I send emails. There’s no way to get a hold of them on the weekend, and they’re like, oh, you can transfer that details on Monday. Well, I’m like, I’m flying to Fiji before then, so I kind of just rolled the dice and hoped it worked out.

It feels like there were more options on the table than "see what happens," especially since he was staying with his girlfriend, who might've been able to call on his behalf. I guess I shouldn't be surprised that the same guy who gave a guy a case of beer to teach him to swim would have this kind of casual attitude about all of his things.

Kilby goes on Survivor, has a memorable run, gains a love of aquadumping, but ultimately gets voted out next to Kristin Flickinger. Of course, as a part of the jury, he didn't return home until Season 51 was over. Kilby picked up things from there:

I get back to Canada, the first email I read was, hey, we were not able to reach you, so your stuff is going up for auction unless you pay like $2000 in storage fees or whatever. And I went, I can’t afford 2000 bucks right now, so that sucks. But then I was like, wait, what if I bid at an auction on my own stuff? I made my own Storage Wars, you know what I mean?

He had just gotten off of one of the best reality shows, and he wanted to recreate the experience from another show. Granted, the stakes were much higher on Storage Wars, as Kilby planned on trying to outbid competitors on all of his belongings to get a discount.

Unfortunately, he didn't win that Survivor money, and as such, didn't have a ton to spare for the auction. Readers can guess where things are headed, but it's great to hear him recap how it all went down:

It goes up to 400 bucks. And that’s about as much as I had…Part of me had this whole like after Survivor, I’m just like a minimalist now, man. I don’t need stuff. I lost the bid to my own stuff, so somebody named Prince C now owns all of my belongings, my couch, my cheetah painting where he’s dressed as a general. I called him 'General Cheetah.'

The wildest part of this story is that Kilby only had $400 dollars, and according to a photo he shared on TikTok, the winning bid was $442. Couldn't he have found a friend or family member to float him an extra hundred? I can't imagine losing everything in my apartment over less than $50.

Learning this makes me think Kilby had a worse exit from Survivor than both Rhode Island Rob and Brady. How can you go on a reality show to win money and leave with a lot less than you started with? Maybe this story will convince Jeff Probst to bring him back sooner rather than later, so he can get a new couch or a portrait of a cheetah dressed as a general.

Kilby is like the poster boy for Survivor's changes to casting in Season 51, and I'm here for it. Finding people who were capable of risking it all to win was a good call, and it's resulted in some real chaos. So chaotic, in fact, people were discussing eating corn from poop, but fortunately even the wilder players shied away from that.

Catch new episodes of Survivor on CBS on Wednesdays at 8:00 p.m. ET. With these latest eliminations, I'm not sure who will end up winning it all. I will say I have no shortage of favorites, however, and wouldn't mind seeing a few people take home the grand prize.

#3533. Eight 'Winter Arc' Rules That Will Actually Deliver Results

There are a lot of terrible social media trends out there aimed at self-improvement, yet even though everybody has been making fun of the "Winter Arc" craze, I actually think it’s a good one. During your Winter Arc, you promise yourself you’ll stick to your fitness and self-care routines during (and despite) the end-of-year chaos. It's a good goal, with one caveat: Make sure you choose rules that will actually improve your life and deliver results.

Think of the “arc” in the sense of a “story arc.” The Winter Arc is a self-improvement journey that unfolds over the last few months of the calendar year. The most hardcore #gymtok-ers will tell you the Winter Arc officially begins on Oct. 1, but others start in early November, or whenever they get around to it. The "when" isn't critical, though—whenever you read this is a fine time to start. The close of the Winter Arc is fixed, however: It ends Jan. 1, just as everybody who is less dedicated than you is waking from their holiday food comas and resolving to get in shape.

You get to choose your own terms for your Winter Arc. The general vibe is one of locking in, committing to your goals, and actually doing the things you’re always saying you’ll do. TikToker @carlyupgraded has said that her own mental image of someone nailing their Winter Arc is “hood up, headphones on, getting ready to go for a run in the rain at 5 a.m.”

It turns out I’ve accidentally been Winter-Arc-ing for years; I just didn’t know it had a catchy name. Why save your gym routine for New Year’s when you’ll have the place to yourself all December? We’re even gifted with an extra hour in the mornings to fill with something productive.

I really love the mindset shift involved. Commonly, people are active in the summer (great time for outdoor fun), may or may not stick with their routines in the fall, and let everything fall apart as the holidays approach. Who has time to go to the gym when you’re planning Thanksgiving, attending holiday parties, studying for final exams, or whatever else the end of the year throws in front of you?

But that’s the exact reason why this time of year is the best to start (or restart) a fitness routine, or really any kind of routine. When you start a routine during a busy time of year, you’ll be forced to make it sustainable. The gym routine you can stick with amid the chaos isn’t going to be one you drop after a few months. You’re already training yourself to work around obstacles as they come up, which is a key component of self-efficacy. And when the chaos clears on Jan. 1, your routine will be even easier to stick to.

Of course, there are ways to lean in too hard: Choosing unsustainable habits, falling for bad diet advice, mistaking not masturbating for some kind of health hack, the usual suspects. There’s also the pitfall of focusing too much on the vibes and too little on what you’re actually going to do or how you’ll benefit.

And then there’s the framing: You were working on yourself all year, but you’re in danger of letting up on the gas, but you’re committed to locking in so that you’re a step ahead of everybody who takes this time to slack off. I really don’t love this tack. Self-improvement is not a competition. There’s a difference between being consistent in your training and healthy eating (good) and seeing the pursuit of health and fitness as something where you always have to work harder because you’re at risk of getting left behind.

I also don’t love how gendered the Winter Arc TikToks tend to be. When you search for Winter Arc content, the first few suggestions include “winter arc for women” and “winter arc for men.” When I first started looking at the Winter Arc trend a few years ago, the women’s versions were more likely to include restrictive dieting or to focus on how the Winter Arc will finally (sigh) snatch your waist. These days, the focus is more on personal goal setting: Lots of the girlies filming their Winter Arc rules are doing so in a notebook and talking about journaling exercises that will help you identify what you need to work on to get to your "best self." Sometimes this is all monetized; training plans and journaling prompts can, of course, be purchased at the link in bio.

I do like that many of the women’s versions emphasize sustainability and setting your own goals rather than copying somebody else's. I don't love the enormity of the mental burden you're supposed to shoulder before even beginning. Should I really have to file an in-depth written report with myself before revamping every area of my life with a 100% commitment to multiple goals?

The men’s versions tend to go off the rails in another direction, with rules like “no girls” or “go ghost.” No distractions! Here, I've seen a shift over the years as well: at first there was overly serious content, followed quickly by satire (yelling at the viewer to get divorced and go work out in the dark). Now the men's videos tend to be more vibes-based, featuring images of pre-dawn workouts and plates full of salad with motivational quotes playing in the background. When the men give their rules, they tend to be simpler than the women's—no journaling exercises—but they often boil down to the same overly strict routines. (And then, of course, they'll offer to sell you a 90-day or 60-day plan.)

If you’re going to do a Winter Arc (or if you’re already doing one), make sure to structure it in a way that benefits you. Choosing 10 overly ambitious goals and setting yourself up for failure is not a healthy way to approach self-improvement, OK? Pick goals that are meaningful, achievable without divine intervention, and trackable with tools you already have at hand (for example, tracking your steps with a Fitbit or your running mileage with a Garmin watch).

It’s also helpful to think of developing yourself over this arc, rather than taking it as a three-month (or two-month) challenge where you have to do everything right all the time. If you currently wake up at 8 a.m. and want to wake up at 5 a.m., you don’t have to set your alarm for 5 a.m. tomorrow. It’s OK to aim for 7:30 a.m., make that a habit, then try for 7:00 a.m., and so on.

With that in mind, here are some "rules" I've seen from creators that I'm actually on board with (so long as you don't overwhelm yourself with them):

Wake up earlier. A great goal, especially if you take advantage of the time change to make things easier on your body.

Get to bed on time. Never a bad idea. Cultivating good sleep habits in general is always worthwhile.

Get your steps in. Be thoughtful about what your target is: 10,000 is not for everybody. Better to choose a number that would be a modest improvement on what you already do.

Exercise X times per week. Pick a number that works for you, and get into it. Be realistic about your goal, and for the best results, be consistent even if you’re sore at first.

Eat healthy. This is a great goal, with the major caveat that there are a lot of ways to eat healthy. You don’t need to cut out sugar or pretend that there’s something evil about seed oils. Do get more protein and veggies.

Be more thoughtful about using social media. I’m not going to tell you to delete all your apps (“except TikTok,” as the TikTokers say). But it’s fair to consider whether you might want to delete a few apps, turn off some notifications, or put your phone on Do Not Disturb for more hours of the day.

Journal or read more. Journaling can be great for working through your feelings or cultivating a creative habit. Reading can be entertainment or a great way to learn. Choose whichever you need most.

Learn a new skill. I’ve mostly seen this one in the men’s TikToks, and I love it. They’re often thinking of “skills” that will help in some kind of entrepreneurship grift they’re about to sell you, but there are tons of skills that will come in handy in life, or that are at least fun to learn. Practice a language, get better at cooking, make some art. Skills are, as I’ve noted, a multi-layered exercise for your brain. And they may come in handy someday.

This year I've slacked off on my fitness routine as I've gotten more involved in other hobbies, but I'm actually looking forward to being more consistent. My winter goals include exercising early in the day when possible and reading 20 minutes each day. (I'm even tracking the second one with a sticker chart.)

#3532. High School Teacher Arrested for Allegedly Planning to Have Sex With Girl, 15

A high school teacher in Pennsylvania was arrested after he allegedly made arrangements online to have sex with a 15-year-old girl, who was actually an undercover officer.

Fayette County District Attorney Michael Aubele said that Lester Eugene Everly II allegedly arranged to meet up and pay for sex during an online conversation with an officer, whom he believed was an adult offering him the opportunity to have sex with a 15-year-old girl they knew, according to WTAE.

Aubele went on to explain how they caught Everly, 47, in the act.

“Our police officer was posing as a person who had a girlfriend who had a 15-year-old child that he could make available for $170,” Aubele said in a statement. “So the defendant traveled to this location, South Union Township, brought other things that he was asked to bring with him, that he would need for sexual activity. We were able to confirm that this was the individual that we believed we were speaking to online.”

Everly was arrested on Saturday, November 14, as part of the undercover operation that the Pennsylvania State Police Uniontown Criminal Investigation Unit and the PSP Bureau of Criminal Investigation Computer Crime Unit ran together.

After Everly was taken into custody, police said he confessed to bringing a condom and $180 to the meetup location he previously arranged with the officer.

Everly is currently in custody at Fayette County Prison. His preliminary hearing is scheduled to take place on November 23.

In light of the scandal, Everly has been identified as a teacher at Albert Gallatin High School in Fayette County, Pennsylvania.

Following Everly’s arrest, Albert Gallatin Interim Superintendent Dr. Jason Hutchinson issued a statement regarding the citation.

“Albert Gallatin has been informed of the arrest of a staff member last evening. The safety and security of our students is always the District’s primary concern, and will be the District’s focus as this matter proceeds,” Hutchinson said, per the outlet. “The District is cooperating with law enforcement and is unable to comment further.”

It’s not currently clear whether Everly has entered a plea or retained legal counsel following his arrest. The Pennsylvania State Police did not immediately respond to Us’ request for comment when contacted about updates in the case.

Parents, teachers and guardians interested in learning more about protecting children from exploitation can find useful tools and information at Know2Protect.

#3530. Casting Walter White: How ‘Breaking Bad’ Found Bryan Cranston

While the Breaking Bad universe would eventually expand to include dozens of characters, the pilot was actually a tidy affair. At its center was Walter White, whose journey would require an actor of extraordinary depth and nuance. It’s not an exaggeration to say that the success or failure of Breaking Bad would rest primarily on his sagging shoulders.

SHARON BIALY, casting director: I don’t know if Bryan knows this, but when Sherry [Bialy] and I went in to meet with Vince to try to get the job as casting directors—­our “audition”—­we literally said, “You may think we’re crazy. We hope you don’t fire us before you hire us. But what about Bryan Cranston?” And he said, “By golly, that’s who I want. I worked with him on The X-­ Files.”

Sherry and I did a lot of theater at the time. We were doing Aaron Sorkin’s new play [The Farnsworth Invention], and Bryan came in and read. We were blown away. He was so talented on Malcolm in the Middle, obviously, but this was live theater with a lot of language. Anyway, Bryan didn’t get the role, but his audition was incredible. And I never forgot it.

VINCE GILLIGAN, creator: Bryan was the only guy I was thinking of when I wrote the script. I had written an episode of The X-­ Files called “Drive,” which came out in 1998, and I was lucky enough to hire him to play the bad guy.

We were really struggling to cast this role because we needed a guy who could be really scary, someone who could make us feel like our hero, Agent Mulder, could get his head blown off at any second. But also, he had to be kind of an asshole. [Throughout the episode] he’s ranting about the government. He’s ranting about stuff like, “Agent Mulder— is that a Jewish name?”

He’s a thoroughly unlikable guy. And yet you had to feel bad for him, for what happens to him at the end of the episode. You had to feel sympathy.

We only had a day or two left before production was going to start. We were going to have to settle on somebody. We had plenty of actors come in who were scary as all get out, but they weren’t necessarily likable. And then this guy walks in the door: Bryan Cranston. Never heard of him before. And he nails it in the audition. As he left, we all stood up and shook his hand, and then I looked to the other producers and to Rick Millikan, our casting director, and I said, “Off to wardrobe!” He was that good.

When I came up with the idea of Breaking Bad, I thought, This is a guy who, again, is going to be very unlikable. He’s going to do a lot of unlikable things, and the audience still has to sympathize with him. Who would be good for this role? I know! That guy, Bryan Cranston. And I wrote it for him. I never really had anyone else in mind.

MELISSA BERNSTEIN, co-executive producer: He was in an episode of X-­Files, playing this racist, and somehow, over the course of the episode, you go from loathing him to feeling badly that he doesn’t make it. He just was able to make someone so unsavory be human. Vince also said, “And he’s so great with comedy. I just feel it in my bones that he could bring those chops to drama—­his sense of timing, the way he embodies those choices physically. He’s perfect.”

BRYAN CRANSTON: I instruct young actors all the time that without a healthy dose of luck, you will not have a career. And this [episode of The X-­ Files] was a lucky break for me.

I had just gotten back from shooting this little movie that I wrote and directed, called Last Chance. I spent all of our money on it, and by the end I was like, Wow, what are we doing on this film? But we rolled the dice on it, and now I was back in town and got a call from my agent about an audition. I said, “Whatever it is, let me know, because I really could use the money.” It just so happened that my look at the time, from this movie that I did, was a perfect look for this guy [on The X-­Files]. So, I went in, and I got the job—­and I was grateful for it.

It’s only in retrospect that I realized Vince Gilligan wanted to see me [to discuss Breaking Bad] was because I had played this reprehensible character that, despite his actions, still needed the audience to root for his life. Despite the despicable person in the back seat, David Du­chovny’s humanity would not allow him to just pull over and say, “Fuck it, die. You’re a horrible human being. I just want you to die.” He couldn’t do it. That’s really, in a nutshell, what Vince Gilligan does.

I knew intuitively that coming off seven years of a comedy, I needed to look for a drama. If I didn’t, I could have been typecast. If you want to expand on the opportunities that may present themselves, you need to take control. I was offered a couple of comedy pilots that I turned down, and I was perfectly willing to wait. Then Breaking Bad came into my lap.

I read it . . . and I couldn’t believe it. I was stunned. I thought, This is perhaps the best hour­-long screenplay that I’ve ever read. I felt tremendous empathy for this character. This poor guy who is just struggling. And I was the same age as Walter White—­I was fifty.

But reading the pilot, I didn’t know where it was going. You have this fish­ out­ of­ water teacher, cooking crystal meth? How could that possibly be sustained year after year after year? How can someone who knows nothing about that world survive? And Vince explained that he wanted to turn Mr. Chips into Scarface.

In the same way that The Sopranos is unthinkable with someone other than James Gandolfini in the role of Tony Soprano, I can’t get my head around the idea of a version of Breaking Bad that doesn’t include Bryan Cranston. But this is Hollywood, and even on basic cable, you don’t just sign up a former sitcom star—­ not even one as gifted as Bryan—­and hand him the starring role in a complex drama without a bit of, shall we say . . . discussion.

MARK JOHNSON, executive producer: Obviously, some people came up for Walter White who were names, but we never got around to entertaining them seriously. It was Vince’s idea to cast him. And despite the fact that there wasn’t a unanimous wave of approval, there wasn’t the kind of pushback that you’d probably have today, in large part because I don’t think the expectation was that we were going to get any real name, any big name.

MELISSA BERNSTEIN: AMC had found Jon Hamm for Mad Men, and they sort of got to reintroduce him to the business. I think they thought we would do something similar with Bryan.

CHARLIE COLLIER, president, general manager, AMC: I was never in the room when they were debating the cast with Vince and Mark. That would have been the programming group. And then they would come back to us and say, “They want that father from Malcolm in the Middle.” And we’d be like, “Really? He’s going to be the linchpin for this whole ambitious project?”

CHRISTINA WAYNE, senior VP, scripted programming, AMC: When Vince suggested Bryan, we all kind of said, “That guy from Malcolm in the Middle?” And then he started showing us a bunch of tape of Bryan in other things, and I was, like, Oh my God—­he’s a total chameleon.

JAMIE ERLICHT, co­-president, Sony Pictures Television: It’s funny. This is one of those great Hollywood stories that has been told so many times. You sit on the sidelines and watch, and it takes on a life of its own. That life is a little different than the truth, sure, but it’s a better story.

The story is that Zack [Van Amburg] and I heard “Bryan Cranston,” and we were really unsure, and we tried to convince Vince that, No, that’s not the way to go. That’s part of a story about how despite all the forces against him, Bryan Cranston became Walter White.

It’s a great story. I love that story. I mean, I don’t love that story.

The truth is, the show was going forward. We weren’t worried about the writing because Vince was knocking it out of the park. The directing? We weren’t worried about the directing. The casting was going to be the next critical element. If you don’t have it—­ well, it’s funny to think about it now. With ninety­ nine point nine percent of other actors in that role, that show is just a well­ written good show that doesn’t become the legacy show that it’s become. And so Vince brought up Bryan Cranston.

I had worked with Bryan on King of Queens. He was the wacky neighbor, a guest star. I was a mid­ level executive, and I was in charge of that show. I always thought he brought a lot of comedic value, just like he did on Seinfeld, and obviously Malcolm in the Middle.

So, when the name Bryan Cranston came up, I was like, Hmmm, that’s interesting. I’ve never seen him do the more dramatic stuff. Do you think he can do it?

Vince was very passionate. He said he had worked with him on X-­Files, and that’s where he really saw what he was capable of on the drama side. We said, “Great, would you send us the X-­Files episode?” Which he did. I remember it was the next day. Zack and I were watching it. We looked at each other and said, “It’s a little bit of a leap of faith, but Vince is passionate, and Bryan is truly talented. Sure, we’re in.” The process took all of thirty­ six hours.

That version of the story, the true version of the story, is not as sexy as the one where Bryan jumped through thirty­ nine hoops and almost didn’t get cast. But that’s how it happened.

ZACK VAN AMBURG, co­-president, Sony Pictures Television: Remember, at this point, Michael Chiklis had gone from doing comedy to being a badass antihero (in The Shield). So, on one hand, you worry: Wait, are we just pulling a page out of the same playbook? Let’s take another sitcom guy and have him do a dark drama.

I think Vince was really clear on why he wanted Bryan. There was a likability factor that was undeniable. There was also a sort of sympathy that Bryan was able to elicit. And Vince also said, “No, wait a second—­ this guy’s also a dramatic actor.”

While some of this stuff gets lost in the haze of time—­ and the internet has a way of transforming rumors into something disguised as fact—­ it’s fair to say that Bryan was always the first choice for the role of Walter White. Regardless of what you may have heard, no one else was offered the job. Not Matthew Broderick, not John Cusack. No one. But you can’t fault anyone for doing their due diligence.

SHARON BIALY: The network likes names. They want to talk about other names. We did that. We did a couple of auditions and meetings. We just met recently with an actor on something else, and he reminded me that he was in the waiting room when Bryan walked out, and he turned to the other three actors and said, “We should all just go home. It’s over. That guy’s going to get it.”

VINCE GILLIGAN: We saw a lot of really good actors, several of them now famous names. They never dissuaded me that Bryan was the guy. And luckily, Bryan said yes, because he was up at the same time for a pilot for Fox that was going to pay him . . . well, my understanding is, substantially more money. Like a doctor show. Thank goodness he went with us instead.

#3528. RedMagic 11S Pro review: Active liquid and fan cooling meets aggressive pricing

The RedMagic 11S Pro isn’t trying to beat mainstream flagships. Instead, it wins over mobile gamers with active liquid-and-fan cooling, sharp AMOLED display, and 19+ hour battery life at an unbeatable $799 starting price. But it does come with its shortcomings.

Chipset underperforms against flagship rivals

Low light camera performance underperforms

Why you can trust Tom's Guide Our writers and editors spend hours analyzing and reviewing products, services, and apps to help find what's best for you. Find out more about how we test, analyze, and rate.

From the iPhone 18 Pro Max to the Galaxy S26 Ultra, I’ve tested virtually every major flagship phone released this year. They’re all striking in their own way, but they generally follow the same blueprint of what makes them the best phone contenders.

The RedMagic 11S Pro is a departure from the norm, leaning closer to a niche phone that prioritizes gaming above all else. That really shows in its radical design, which pairs a flagship Snapdragon processor with an active liquid-and-fan cooling system built to keep frame rates consistently smooth.

After testing it for a week, I can tell you that this over-the-top hardware offers fair value and comes in at a price that easily undercuts every mainstream flagship on the market. Here's how.

50MP main (f/1.8), 50MP ultrawide (f/2), 2MP macro (f/2.4)

6.45 in x 3.01 in x 0.35 inches (163.82 x 76.54 x 8.9 mm)

Nightfreeze (transparent black,) Subzero (transparent silver)

While most flagship phones look alike with their respective camera housings on the back, the RedMagic 11S Pro leans hard into its gaming PC-inspired aesthetic. In fact, there’s nothing different about its design compared to the previous RedMagic 11 Pro from earlier this year — boasting a flat metal frame and boxy lines that give it a dense build quality that feels substantial in hand.

I'm particularly mesmerized by the design on the back of the phone, as the brushed aluminum material behind the glass panel and flush camera housing are a radical departure. And with subtle RGB accents, a visible liquid-cooling loop, and an LED-lit fan, the whole package makes it look more like a miniature custom PC rig than a conventional smartphone.

Most flagship phones get toasty during extended play, usually after 15 minutes of demanding 3D gaming, which leads to thermal throttling — but that’s not an issue with the RedMagic 11S Pro. By combining its upgraded AquaCore liquid-cooling loop with a high-speed 24,000 RPM fan, it actively pulls heat away from the overclocked Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 Leading Version chip to keep sustained performance intact.

Even after 30 minutes of dungeon hunting in Diablo Immortal and killing time with Call of Duty Mobile, the phone remains noticeably cooler to the touch than mainstream flagships. Best of all, I don’t see dropped frame rates like I do on other phones.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

As much as I love gaming on the RedMagic 11S Pro’s 6.85-inch AMOLED display, watching videos on it is just as satisfying. This panel produces colors that pop with deep saturation, and alongside a 144Hz refresh rate that keeps UI animations fluid, it actually holds up well outdoors. In our lab testing, the panel reached a peak brightness of 1,950 nits, beating RedMagic’s own 1,800-nit rating and making it easy to view under the harsh midday sun.

You wouldn’t know it just by looking at its sleek 8.9 mm profile, but the RedMagic 11S Pro packs a massive 7,500 mAh silicon-carbon battery inside. In our battery drain test, it lasted an impressive 19 hours and 47 minutes, easily cruising through a full day of normal use in my experience — with plenty of gas left in the tank by night’s end.

When I do finally need to plug in, its 80W wired charging gets it back to 60% in just 30 minutes from a dead battery. Another feature I really appreciate is that RedMagic lets me activate the internal fan to optimize charging and reduce heat buildup.

Perhaps the most surprising thing about the RedMagic 11S Pro isn’t its liquid cooling or its overclocked Snapdragon chip — it’s how little it costs. Starting at $799 for the 12GB/256GB model and going up to $899 for the 16GB/512GB variant, it’s a flagship-caliber phone for hundreds less.

It comes equipped with a top-tier chipset, a massive 7,500 mAh battery, and active thermal hardware, which makes the $1,299+ cost of other flagships look bloated. Even against value-minded flagships like the OnePlus 15, the RedMagic 11S Pro still comes in at a lower entry price without cutting corners on raw power. And yes, it’s unlocked right from the get-go!

In order to hit that $799 price point, RedMagic doesn’t offer a triple-camera system — you just get two usable rear sensors: a 50MP main camera and a 50MP ultrawide. It clearly forgoes a dedicated telephoto lens, and as a result, zooming tops out at 10x digital zoom. At that maximum, photos come out extremely soft, muddy, and practically useless.

Low-light photography is a mixed bag too because, while the main sensor does a respectable job of keeping image noise under control, the overall picture comes out noticeably dark and underexposed. Under ideal lighting conditions, though, it captures usable shots worthy of posting on social media.underexposed. Under ideal lighting conditions, though, it captures usable shots worthy of posting on social media.

Even if the RedMagic 11S Pro has the same hardware found in other flagships and is built to last for years, the software support window is regrettably short — and a big reason why some people might pass it over.

Under RedMagic’s official update policy, the 11S Pro is guaranteed just two major Android OS upgrades, which effectively puts it at Android 18 given that it still ships with Android 16. You do get three years of security patches, but that’s still far too short for a phone of this caliber.

Given that Samsung and Google now promise seven years of full OS and security support, RedMagic’s commitment feels painfully short.

Despite packing the overclocked Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 Leading Version chip, the RedMagic 11S Pro kinda underperforms in some synthetic benchmark tests. The phone averaged Geekbench 7 scores of 3,138 in single-core and 7,616 in multi-core, which trails rival Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 flagships by a noticeable margin.

Switching into RedMagic’s high-performance Rise mode, however, dramatically improves the multi-core score up to 10,725, though single-core performance unexpectedly dips to 2,016 in the process.

Fortunately, those weak Geekbench numbers don't tell the whole story when you're actually gaming. In the 3DMark Wild Life Extreme Stress Test, the RedMagic 11S Pro achieved a stability score of 79.4% — matching the iPhone 18 Pro Max. In real-world gameplay, performance remains strong, holding high frame rates for extended stretches without dipping.

I know very well that the RedMagic 11S Pro isn’t trying to beat the Galaxy S26 Ultra or iPhone 18 Pro Max at being an all-purpose flagship. It succeeds by prioritizing mobile gamers, seeing that it delivers standout hardware you simply won’t find elsewhere at $799.

You do have to accept clear trade-offs to get that value. Its synthetic performance scores trail rival flagships out of the box, the dual-camera setup tops out at a soft 10x digital zoom and struggles under low light, and RedMagic’s two-year major OS update policy falls well short of mainstream competitors.

Still, if you want a dedicated gaming powerhouse with unmatched endurance and thermal control at a fraction of the cost, the RedMagic 11S Pro is easily worth getting.

#3527. Your Android Can Get Hacked Without You Doing Anything at All

You probably know that clicking suspicious links online or opening attachments from strangers in an email or text is a recipe for hacking. It's a dangerous world out there online, so it's always important to be vigilant. However, the danger doesn't always involve something you do. There are ways to hack your devices without requiring any intervention on your part whatsoever—and one such example is likely plaguing your Android device right now.

As reported by The Hacker News, there is a critical Android security flaw that could enable remote code execution on your device. In other words, bad actors could use the flaw to run their own code on your phone, effectively taking over the device for their own gain. The flaw, identified as CVE-2026-58868, isn't universal, but it is widespread: It currently affects Android 14 through Android 17, the latest version of Google's OS. If your phone runs Android 12 or Android 13, it may be unaffected, as Google doesn't identify these versions in its security bulletin, but it doesn't explicitly rule them out, either.

There are two silver linings here, however. One, Google hasn't confirmed any active exploits for this security flaw. While that isn't a guarantee that bad actors have missed this exploit so far, it at least opens that possibility. As such, there may be time for users to patch their devices before hackers truly take advantage of the flaw. Second, Google does have a patch for the flaw. The patch may not be available to you right away, however, as it's up to both the manufacturer of your phone and your carrier to issue these updates. Still, a patch is, at the very least, on its way.

This flaw is perhaps the most important to fix, but it's not the only serious issue. In all, Google's latest bulletin highlights 216 vulnerabilities, and, of those, 23 are "critical." As The Hacker News explains, two other of those critical flaws could also allow remote code execution when exploited.

To see whether the patch is installed on your end, open the Settings app on your phone, tap "About phone" or "About tablet," then choose the Android version on-screen. Look for a date of "2026-11-01" or later. All security patches from Nov. 1 and on will fix this issue. If not, you'll ned to wait for the patch.

It’s no secrets that celebrities can be major superfans, even getting starstruck or seeking out advice from their acting heroes. Though this may be the first time I’ve heard of an actor trolling a celebrity who isn’t the Rock poking fun at friend Kevin Hart. I didn’t expect Off Campus’ Stephen Kalyn to admit he trolled Timothèe Chalamet HARD at the beginning of his career.

The actor’s career has since taken off thanks to his starring role as Dean Di Laurentis in the hockey romance series. Before that he had a recurring role in shows like Gen V and Motorheads, and apparently, he admired Chalamet’s career and reached out to the Dune actor for tips. It reached the point that his "trolling" became a bit. The Elite Daily shares what the actor had to say about his DMing days:

This is, like, kind of embarrassing. I went on Instagram and I DM’d him, and I was like, ‘Hey, man! Just letting you know, I’m new in the business, and if you have any tips or whatever, let a guy know. I really loved your work in Call Me By Your Name, Beautiful Boy.’ He never responded to me.

The actor clearly has no problems being totally open even if it could be embarrassing. Honestly, I respect it. While his former pastime is a little "unhinged," I doubt Chalamet even noticed given he probably gets MANY messages from fans. Though I don’t blame Kalyn for admiring the actor’s confidence or how fast his career seemed to take off. His admiration is clearly being channeled into his many shirtless scenes on Off Campus, which he has shared can be a little “uncomfortable” at times though leaves him feeling ready to conquer the world. Definitely Chalamet-level energy.

However, his admission had a mix of reactions from fans in the comments. Some understand Kalyn’s admiration, such as kandiboober who shares, “I text him a lot too. Usually, I send him pie recipes and grocery lists.” Others feel like it’s the equivalent of texting a celebrity happy birthday when you know you won’t get a response. Though for a while a lack of response didn’t stop Kalyn from checking in “every month,” as he continues:

It just became a bit at that point. I was like ‘hey, man, you up?’ or ‘hey, what’s up? You gonna respond to that DM?’

The actor doesn’t say how long the "trolling" lasted. However, a few fans feel like he could have kept that information to himself. Although this isn’t the strangest thing a celebrity has done or even the most dedicated. We can’t forget Emma Stone’s wild story about trying to catching a glimpse of a Real Housewife. As far as I know Kalyn has yet to cross paths with Chalamet in person. Though given his career is on the rise there could be a time when they’ll be on the same red carpet and he’ll have a chance to speak to him.

In the meantime, Kalyn is busy filming Season 2 of Off Campus and even doing commercials for Verizon, which is set to premiere in April 2027. So for now, it seems his pastime ‘trolling’ has fallen to the side.

You can catch up on Season 1 and see every shirtless moment with an Amazon Prime subscription. However, Chalamet doesn't make an appearance in the popular series.

#3525. 'Ocarina of Time' for Switch 2 Might Already Have a Weird Glitch

Thursday is a big day for Zelda fans. That's when the remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time officially launches on Switch 2, marking the first major linear (i.e., non-open-world) 3D Zelda game since the 2016 Twilight Princess remake on Wii U. I, for one, have been waiting for this day for years. I loved the N64 original and the 3DS remake, so to have the chance to play a modern take on the definitive Zelda is so exciting—that is, if it actually runs as it should.

I stumbled upon this interesting post on X from Austin John Plays, a YouTuber with a host of Zelda coverage. According to Austin John Plays, Ocarina of Time already ships with a weird glitch that won't necessarily break your experience, but which may slow it down for a while, and perhaps even confuse players into thinking something is wrong with their game or their console.

As his post explains, if you're playing the physical copy of Ocarina of Time, and it's the first game you've ever played on your Switch 2—maybe you got one of those fancy new Zelda anniversary consoles and want to break it in properly?—you may run into glaring performance issues: The game may freeze, your controller may stop working, and the FPS may drop to single digits.

Luckily, Austin John Plays says the fix is easy: just wait. Eventually, your game will boot back to the title screen. When it does, don't try to play right away. Instead, close the game, restart your Switch 2, then try relaunching Ocarina of Time. Austin John Plays advises you may need to repeat this process two or three times, but after that, you shouldn't continue to run into issues. I wouldn't be surprised if Nintendo releases a patch right away for this glitch if it turns out to be as widespread as this post implies.

However, seeing as the game doesn't come out until tomorrow, there's something you can do to prevent it. Austin John Plays thinks the bug only impacts Switch 2 consoles that haven't run other games before. If you've had your console a while, you're likely set. But if you just bought the 40th anniversary Zelda edition of the Switch 2, you might not have had a chance to run a game on it yet. As such, download a game from the e-shop—even a free demo—just to get the system running. Hopefully, that will be enough to circumvent the glitch, and prevent issues when Ocarina of Time launches tomorrow.
